nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Title: Spectroscopic Reflectometry Film Thickness & Edge Bead Uniformity Metrology
**Hierarchy Level:** Metrology (Leaf Step)  
**Process Node:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Target Material:** Shipley 1813 Positive Photoresist on Silicon / Dielectric Substrates  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Equipment & Consumables Required
- Spectroscopic reflectometer / optical thin-film metrology station with automated wafer stage.
- Calibration standards: Bare silicon reference substrate and certified standard oxide wafer ($SiO_2$ on $Si$).
- Process wafer: $100\text{ mm}$ wafer with spin-coated Shipley 1813 resist (post-softbake at $115^\circ\text{C}$).
- Metrology software loaded with Cauchy/Sellmeier dispersion models for Shipley 1813 and optical constants ($n(\lambda)$, $k(\lambda)$).

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```
+------------------------------------+
| 1. System Calibration              |
|    - Dark & baseline silicon scan  |
+-----------------+------------------+
                  |
                  v
+------------------------------------+
| 2. Recipe & Dispersion Modeling    |
|    - Cauchy / Sellmeier parameter  |
+-----------------+------------------+
                  |
                  v
+------------------------------------+
| 3. Multi-Point Wafer Mapping       |
|    - Automated 9-point or 49-point |
|    - Film thickness profile        |
+-----------------+------------------+
                  |
                  v
+------------------------------------+
| 4. Edge Bead Exclusion Metrology   |
|    - Radial profile scan to edge   |
|    - Verify PGMEA EBR clearance    |
+------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Baseline Calibration
1. Mount the certified bare silicon reference wafer onto the reflectometer vacuum chuck.
2. Acquire the dark current spectrum ($I_{\text{dark}}$) with the illumination shutter closed.
3. Open the shutter and perform specular reflection calibration against the certified bare silicon standard across the UV-visible spectrum ($350\text{ nm} - 800\text{ nm}$).

#### Step 2: Optical Dispersion Model Setup
1. Define the film stack in the optical analysis software: $\text{Air} \rightarrow \text{Shipley 1813 Photoresist} \rightarrow \text{Silicon Substrate}$ (or underlying thermal oxide layer).
2. Apply the Cauchy dispersion equation for transparent organic resist:
   $$n(\lambda) = A + \frac{B}{\lambda^2} + \frac{C}{\lambda^4}$$
3. Set the nominal target seed thickness to $1.30\ \mu\text{m}$ ($1300\text{ nm}$) with extinction coefficient $k(\lambda) \approx 0$ in the non-absorbing visible range.

#### Step 3: Multi-Point Radial Wafer Mapping
1. Load the softbaked $100\text{ mm}$ Shipley 1813 wafer onto the measurement chuck and engage vacuum.
2. Program an automated **9-point** or **49-point wafer map** across radial coordinates ($R = 0\text{ mm}, 25\text{ mm}, 45\text{ mm}$).
3. Measure interference fringes and fit the theoretical Fresnel reflection spectrum against measured reflectance to extract film thickness $T_{\text{resist}}$ at each site.
4. Calculate mean thickness ($\bar{T}$) and percent non-uniformity:
   $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{T_{\max} - T_{\min}}{2 \times \bar{T}} \times 100$$

#### Step 4: Edge Bead Removal (EBR) & Edge Uniformity Verification
1. Translate the optical stage radially outwards from radius $R = 45\text{ mm}$ to $R = 50\text{ mm}$ in $0.5\text{ mm}$ increments.
2. Detect the transition boundary where the resist film drops to zero to verify the solvent EBR width and verify there is no residual bead pile-up or clamp contamination risk.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Center & Mean Film Thickness ($\bar{T}$)** | $1.30$ | $\pm 0.015$ ($\pm 15\text{ nm}$) | $\mu\text{m}$ | Cauchy fit optical reflectometry |
| **Measurement Precision** | Baseline repeatability | $\pm 2$ | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic reflectometer repeated-run standard deviation |
| **Wafer Mapping Grid** | 9-point or 49-point | Exact grid execution | points/wafer | Automated optical stage coordinates across $100\text{ mm}$ wafer |
| **Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2 Node)** | Substrate alignment | $\pm 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical stage fiducial alignment / position encoders |

---

### 4. Literature References
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  - Cauchy and Sellmeier optical dispersion modeling for refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$.
  - Photoresist ($1.3\ \mu\text{m}$) measurement precision within $\pm 2\text{ nm}$.
  - Automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping to track radial film non-uniformity across spin coating.
- **Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**:
  - Shipley 1813 spin-coat target thickness of $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\text{ nm}$ across $100\text{ mm}$ wafers.
  - Edge bead removal (EBR) with PGMEA solvent jet to eliminate clamp contamination.
- **Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - Shipley 1813 nominal film thickness of $\sim 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ at $4000\text{ RPM}$ after $115^\circ\text{C}$ softbake.
  - Gen 2 alignment tolerance limit of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
citations: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming (Madou - Fundamentals of Microfabrication)
Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology (Tompkins & Irene - Handbook of Ellipsometry)
Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018) (https://sam.zeloof.xyz/first-ic/)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated PGMEA Solvent Edge Bead Removal (EBR) Dispense Calibration

**Document ID:** `SOP-LITHO-EBR-001`  
**Level/Stage:** Architecture & Integration > Chemical Processing > Wet Chemistry > Photolithography  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm)  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Resist System:** Shipley 1813 Positive Photoresist (DNQ Novolak)  
**Substrate:** 100 mm Silicon Wafer  

---

### Process Flow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Spin Coater Chuck    │
│    Vacuum Verified     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Dynamic Shipley 1813  │
│        Dispense        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Film Thinning Spin   │
│      at 4000 RPM       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Calibrated PGMEA    │
│  Solvent Jet at Wafer  │
│          Edge          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Centrifugal Edge Dry  │
│      & Clamp Bead      │
│  Clearance Inspection  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Preparation & Dehydration:**
   - Transfer the 100 mm silicon wafer to a dehydration convection oven at **150°C to 200°C for 30 minutes** (or flat hot plate at **180°C for 2 minutes**) to desorb physisorbed water molecules.
   - Subject the wafer to HMDS vapor priming for **3 minutes at 120°C** to silylate silanol groups into hydrophobic trimethylsilyl monolayers.

2. **Photoresist Dynamic Dispense:**
   - Mount and verify vacuum chuck hold on the 100 mm wafer.
   - Initiate dynamic dispense of **2 to 3 mL** of Shipley 1813 resist at **500 RPM for 4 to 5 seconds** (spread cycle).

3. **High-Speed Film Uniformity Spin:**
   - Ramp the spin speed at an acceleration of **10,000 RPM/s** up to **4,000 RPM**.
   - Maintain the spin cycle at **4,000 RPM for 30 seconds** to establish a dry film thickness of approximately **1.30 µm to 1.33 µm**.

4. **Automated PGMEA Edge Bead Removal (EBR) Dispense Calibration:**
   - Align the automated solvent dispense nozzle targeted at the wafer bevel margin on the 100 mm substrate to prevent handling clamp contamination.
   - Trigger the calibrated PGMEA (propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate) solvent jet to dissolve and clear the centrifugal edge bead accumulation without impinging on the active central die area.
   - Maintain wafer spin to spin off dissolved residual solvent and dry the perimeter edge boundary prior to deceleration.

5. **Soft Bake (Pre-Bake) Stabilization:**
   - Unload the wafer and place it onto a flat vacuum aluminum hot plate at **115°C for 60 seconds** to drive off 85% of residual casting solvent.

---

### Calibrated Process Metrics

```text
                    Calibrated Physical Parameters      
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │░░░░                                   │
 Film (nm x100)┤░░░░                                   │
               │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒         │
  Soft Bake (C)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒         │
 Dehyd Temp (C)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Spin RPM (x100)┤███████████                            │
               │███████████                            │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
               0.0      37.5     75.0      112.5  150.0 
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Film Thickness (Shipley 1813)** | **1.30 µm** (nominal) | **±15 nm** (or **1.33 µm ± 10 nm**) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Thin-Film Reflectometry across 100 mm substrate |
| **Spin Coater High-Speed Plateau** | **4,000 RPM** | **±0 RPM** (ramp: **10,000 RPM/s**) | Coater Tachometer Optical Encoder |
| **Soft Bake Temperature & Time** | **115°C** | **60 seconds** | Calibrated Vacuum Hot Plate Surface Thermocouple |
| **Gen 1 Macroscopic Alignment Margin** | **±100 µm** | **±0.1 mm** max runout | Optical Projection Stage Alignment Vernier |

---

### Verified Literature Citations

1. **Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**
   - Dehydration bake: 150°C–200°C for 30 minutes.
   - Dispense: 2–3 mL Shipley 1813 at 500 RPM for 5 seconds; ramp at 10,000 RPM/s to 4,000 RPM for 30 seconds.
   - Uniformity: 1.30 µm ± 15 nm across 100 mm wafers.
   - Purpose: PGMEA solvent jet EBR eliminates edge bead to prevent handling clamp contamination.
2. **Source: Positive Photoresist Spin Dynamics, Soft Bake & Development Protocol**
   - Dynamic dispense: 3 mL resist at 500 RPM for 4 seconds; ramp at 10,000 RPM/s to 4,000 RPM for 30 seconds (thickness: 1.33 µm ± 10 nm).
   - Priming: HMDS vapor exposure for 3 minutes at 120°C.
   - Soft Bake: Flat vacuum hot plate at 115°C for 60 seconds (removes 85% of solvent).
3. **Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**
   - Shipley 1813 spin coated at 4,000 RPM (~1.3 µm thickness).
   - Soft bake on flat aluminum hot plate at 115°C for 60 seconds.
   - Gen 1 macro-stage alignment tolerance: ±100 µm (0.1 mm).

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## EBR Arm Trajectory, Flow Rate & Spin-Sync Dispense Recipe Optimization

**Generation Target**: Gen 2 (µm)  
**Process Step**: Photolithography / Edge Bead Removal (EBR) & Resist Conditioning  
**Hierarchy Context**: `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` > `Shipley 1813 Spin Coating, Edge Bead Removal and Softbake` > `Automated PGMEA Solvent Edge Bead Removal (EBR) Dispense Calibration`

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Start: 100mm Wafer   │
│        Chucked         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Spin-Sync        │
│  Acceleration to 1000  │
│          RPM           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   EBR Arm Trajectory   │
│     to Wafer Edge      │
│        R=48.5mm        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   PGMEA Solvent Jet    │
│        Dispense        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Ramp to 4000 RPM    │
│    Final Spin & Dry    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Softbake 115C 60s    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Pre-Conditioning Verification**:
   - Confirm 100 mm silicon wafer has completed dehydration bake at 150°C–200°C for 30 minutes and reactive HMDS vapor priming (silanol silylation into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane bonds).
   - Secure wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the spin coater.

2. **Resist Dispense & Meyerhofer Radial Spread Cycle**:
   - Dispense 2–3 mL of Shipley 1813 positive photoresist at wafer center.
   - Initiate spread cycle: spin at 500 RPM for 5 seconds to uniformly wet the surface before solvent flash evaporation.

3. **Spin-Sync & EBR Arm Trajectory Homing**:
   - Drive the EBR dispensing arm along precision ground linear guide rails (MGN12H) via NEMA 17 stepper drive (1/16 microstepping, ball/lead screw mechanism).
   - Home and position the EBR solvent nozzle over the wafer edge zone (Gen 2 alignment tolerance: $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$, encoder resolution: $1\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Set nozzle dispense angle at 45° directed radially outwards towards wafer bevel edge to eliminate solvent splashback onto the central die area.

4. **Synchronous PGMEA Solvent Dispense**:
   - Trigger the automated PGMEA solvent jet at the peripheral rim while the wafer rotates at a synchronized intermediate spin-speed (800–1,000 RPM).
   - Dispense PGMEA jet for 3–5 seconds to dissolve and clear the peripheral edge bead buildup, preventing clamp contamination during subsequent handling.

5. **Main Spin Thinning & Film Uniformity Ramp**:
   - Retract the EBR arm safely beyond the chuck perimeter.
   - Ramp the spin chuck at 10,000 RPM/s to a terminal speed of 4,000 RPM for 30 seconds to evacuate residual solvent and planarize the resist film.

6. **Post-EBR Softbake**:
   - Transfer wafer immediately to a flat aluminum hot plate.
   - Softbake at 115°C for 60 seconds to drive off volatile casting solvents and stabilize the layer for exposure.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Verification Equipment / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Film Thickness & Uniformity** | $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\ \text{nm}$ ($\sim 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$) | Spectroscopic Reflectometry / Ellipsometry across 100 mm wafer |
| **EBR Arm Stage Positioning Accuracy** | Gen 2 tolerance: $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (Encoder resolution: $1\ \mu\text{m}$) | Linear optical / magnetic encoder feedback along MGN12H rails |
| **Spin Acceleration & Terminal Speed** | Ramp: $10,000\ \text{RPM/s}$; Terminal: $4,000\ \text{RPM} \pm 10\ \text{RPM}$ for $30\ \text{s}$ | Optical tachometer / closed-loop spin chuck servo encoder |
| **Softbake Temperature & Dwell** | $115^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{seconds}$ | Calibrated surface thermocouple on aluminum hot plate |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context Traceability

- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**:
  - *Spin Parameters & Film Profile*: Dispense 2–3 mL Shipley 1813 at 500 RPM for 5 s; ramp at 10,000 RPM/s to 4,000 RPM for 30 s; yielding $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\ \text{nm}$ uniform film on 100 mm wafers.
  - *EBR Chemistry*: Applied PGMEA solvent jet to eliminate edge bead and prevent clamp contamination.
  - *Dehydration & Priming*: Wafer dehydration at 150°C–200°C for 30 min followed by HMDS vapor silylation.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:

  - *Gen 2 Alignment Budget*: Micron-scale feature resolution with Gen 2 stage alignment tolerance of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Precision Linear Stage Design & Vibration Damping**:
  - *Mechanical Architecture*: MGN12H precision linear guide rails, NEMA 17 stepper drive with 1/16 microstepping, straightness $< 5\ \mu\text{m} / 100\ \text{mm}$, and closed-loop optical/magnetic encoder resolution down to $1\ \mu\text{m}$.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** Optical Profilometry & Microscopic Edge Bead Exclusion Zone Metrology  
**Module:** `[Metrology] < [Photolithography]` | **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Metrology Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Wafer Load &      │
│       Centering        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Microscopic Edge    │
│     Exclusion Scan     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     White Light /      │
│  Optical Profilometry  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Bead Profile & Step   │
│   Height Extraction    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria   │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Mounting & Datum Alignment:**
   - Load the post-softbake (115°C, 60 s) 100 mm wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the optical metrology stage.
   - Use microscopic edge detection (Plan Achromat objective, 10x, NA 0.25) to locate the wafer edge bevel and register physical $(X, Y, \theta)$ coordinate zero.

2. **Optical Exclusion Zone Edge Bead Inspection:**
   - Translate the stage radially inward from the physical wafer perimeter toward the active die region.
   - Inspect the PGMEA solvent-cleared boundary under calibrated darkfield/brightfield microscopic illumination to verify clear transition from bare silicon/oxide to continuous photoresist film without solvent splash or residue streaks.

3. **Optical Profilometry & Film Step Height Metrology:**
   - Position the non-destructive optical profilometer / reflectometer head across the cleared transition zone.
   - Execute a line scan from the stripped edge bead exclusion zone across the transition shoulder into the bulk resist.
   - Apply Cauchy optical dispersion modeling to acquire the step-height profile and verify that residual bead build-up is eliminated.

4. **Multi-Point Radial Uniformity Verification:**
   - Transition to automated multi-point (9-point / 49-point) mapping across the 100 mm wafer substrate.
   - Measure nominal bulk Shipley 1813 photoresist thickness and ensure radial film variations stay within tolerance limits prior to UV exposure.

---

```text
Film Tol (±nm)┤▒                                       │
              │▒                                       │
Bulk Film (um)┤███████████                             │
              │███████████                             │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘

```

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bulk Resist Film Thickness** | `1.30 µm` (`~1.3 µm`) | `±15 nm` (within `±2 nm` precision) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry (Cauchy Model) |

  - Optical microscopy resolution setup (10x Plan Achromat, NA 0.25).
  - Gen 2 alignment positioning tolerance limit (`±5 µm`).
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:**

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Metadata
- **Title**: Contact Hotplate Softbake (115°C) & Spectroscopic Reflectometry Resist Thickness Verification
- **Process Line**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Photolithography & Metrology
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type**: Make

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Transfer from   │
│       Spin Chuck       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Contact Hotplate    │
│   Softbake @ 115°C /   │
│          60s           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Active Cooling @ 20°C │
│         / 30s          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Spectroscopic      │
│     Reflectometry      │
│       Alignment        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Cauchy Dispersion    │
│  Model Fit & 9-Point   │
│          Map           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Resist Thickness &   │
│       Uniformity       │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Phase A: Contact Hotplate Softbake
1. **Pre-Bake Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Power on the vacuum-assisted flat aluminum contact hotplate and allow the PID controller to equilibrate at **115°C**.
   - Verify surface temperature across the chuck with a calibrated contact surface probe to ensure thermal gradient stability.
2. **Wafer Transfer & Vacuum Chucking**:
   - Transfer the freshly coated wafer (dispensed with 2–3 mL Shipley 1813 and edge-bead removed) using vacuum tweezers onto the lift pins.
   - Lower the pins to achieve conformal backside contact with the flat aluminum surface and engage vacuum hold-down to prevent air-gap thermal gradients.
3. **Timed Bake Execution**:
   - Execute the softbake cycle for exactly **60 seconds** at **115°C** to drive off residual casting solvents and stabilize the resist matrix.
4. **Post-Bake Chill Cycle**:
   - De-energize chuck vacuum, raise lift pins, and transfer the wafer onto an aluminum chill plate at **20°C** for **30 seconds** to arrest thermal processing before measurement.

---

### Phase B: Spectroscopic Reflectometry Resist Thickness Verification
1. **Optical System Baseline Calibration**:
   - Initialize the spectroscopic reflectometer / ellipsometer light source across the UV-visible inspection band.
   - Run baseline calibration (Dark spectrum and Reference Silicon blank) measuring reflection coefficients:
     $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
2. **Dispersion Modeling Setup**:
   - Select the **Cauchy dispersion model** for Shipley 1813 photoresist parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ over bare silicon substrate.
3. **Automated Wafer Mapping**:
   - Load the baked wafer onto the metrology vacuum stage.
   - Execute an automated **9-point radial wafer map** covering wafer center, mid-radius, and outer edge perimeter exclusion zones.
4. **Data Acquisition & Run Qualification**:
   - Collect reflectance spectra at each point; fit interference oscillation fringes using the Cauchy optical model.
   - Record the extracted thickness values, mean film thickness, and standard deviation across all 9 measurement points.

---

## 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hotplate Surface Bake Temperature** | `115` | `°C` | `±1.0 °C` | Calibrated surface thermocouple probe |
| **Softbake Duration** | `60` | `s` | `±1.0 s` | Integrated tool digital process timer |
| **Mean Photoresist Film Thickness** | `1.30` (1300) | `µm` (`nm`) | `±15 nm` (1.30 µm ± 15 nm) | 9-point spectroscopic reflectometer / ellipsometer |
| **Thickness Measurement Gauge Precision** | `±2` | `nm` | `≤ ±2 nm` | Repeatability fit of Cauchy optical model |

---

## 3. Literature Context Citations

- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - *Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM yields ~1.3 micron thickness.*
  - *Soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds on a flat aluminum hot plate.*
  - *Gen 2 alignment tolerance baseline (±5 microns).*
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  - *Physical principle measuring reflection coefficients $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$.*
  - *Cauchy dispersion model parameterizing $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$.*
  - *Metrology precision for photoresist (1.3 µm measured within ±2 nm).*
  - *Automated 9-point wafer mapping tracking radial film non-uniformity.*
- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**:
  - *Dispense parameters (2–3 mL Shipley 1813).*
  - *Post-spin film uniformity benchmark producing 1.30 µm ± 15 nm across 100mm substrates.*

# Standard Operating Procedure: I-line Stepper Exposure, Post-Exposure Bake and Development Metrology

**Project:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Module:** Photolithography & Metrology (Gen 2: µm scale)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   HMDS Vapor Prime    │
│         120C          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Spin-Coat Shipley   │
│     1813 4000 RPM     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Soft Bake 115C 60s   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    I-line Stepper     │
│    Exposure 365nm     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  MF-319 Development   │
│    45-60s DI Rinse    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Metrology & Overlay  │
│      Inspection       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Dehydration & HMDS Vapor Prime:**
   - Transfer wafer into the primer chamber.
   - Perform Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) vapor prime at **120°C** to promote adhesion on the oxide layer prior to resist dispensing.
2. **Resist Spin Coating:**
   - Dispense Shipley 1813 positive photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
   - Accelerate and spin-coat at **4000 RPM** to establish a nominal resist thickness of **~1.3 µm**.
3. **Soft Bake (Pre-Exposure Bake):**
   - Place wafer onto a calibrated flat aluminum hot plate.
   - Bake at **115°C for 60 seconds** to drive off excess casting solvents and stabilize the film.
4. **I-line Stepper Alignment & Exposure:**
   - Load wafer onto the projection aligner / stepper stage equipped with a 10x Plan Achromat objective (NA 0.25).
   - Perform fiducial mark alignment to align the layer with a tolerance of **≤ ±5 µm** (Gen 2 specification).
   - Expose the pattern using a high-power **365nm i-line UV LED source** or mercury vapor lamp.
5. **Development & Deionized Rinse:**
   - Immerse and gently agitate wafer in **Microposit MF-319 developer** for **45 to 60 seconds**.
   - Immediately quench reaction by transferring into a cascade deionized (DI) water rinse tank for a thorough wash.
   - Blow dry with filtered dry $N_2$.
6. **Critical Dimension (CD) & Alignment Metrology:**
   - Inspect wafer under calibrated optical metrology for feature resolution and residual resist in cleared areas.
   - Measure overlay offsets relative to prior alignment targets.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │■■                                │
Gen 2 Alignment (um)┤■■                                │
                    │██████████████████                │
    Dev Time Max (s)┤██████████████████                │
  Soft Bake Time (s)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
  Soft Bake Temp (C)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Spin Speed (RPM/100)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    28.8     57.5    86.2  115.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Film Thickness** | **1.3** | $\mu\text{m}$ (nominal) | Optical reflectometry / profilometry post 4000 RPM coat |
| **Soft Bake Temperature** | **115** | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ ($\pm 1^{\circ}\text{C}$) | Thermocouple / Pyrometer surface contact sensor |
| **Soft Bake Duration** | **60** | $\text{seconds}$ | Automated hot plate timer |
| **Exposure Wavelength** | **365** | $\text{nm}$ (i-line) | Spectroradiometer / i-line sensor |
| **Development Immersion Time**| **45 – 60** | $\text{seconds}$ | Wet bench chemical immersion timer |
| **Layer Alignment Tolerance** | **$\le \pm 5$** | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical overlay metrology Vernier / split-field microscope |

---

### Literature Citations
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018):** 10x Plan Achromat (NA 0.25) projection optics; Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM (~1.3 µm); soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds; 365nm i-line source; Microposit MF-319 developer for 45–60 s and DI water rinse; Gen 2 alignment target of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse

**Module**: Wet Chemistry / Oxide Patterning  
**Technology Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 1)  
**Classification**: Safety Critical / Hydrofluoric Acid Process  

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 1: Bath Setup & Surfactant    │
│  BOE 6:1 (40% NH4F : 49% HF) + 0.1%  │
│  Triton X-100 / Fluorad @ 25°C       │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 2: Immersion Dip-Etch         │
│  Thermally grown SiO2: 80-100 nm/min │
│  CVD / TEOS SiO2: 150-220 nm/min     │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 3: Cascade Dump Rinse         │
│  5 Cycles UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm)         │
│  Rinse bath cutoff > 16 MOhm-cm      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 4: Endpoint & Metrology       │
│  Hydrophobic dewetting check         │
│  Fluoride neutralization & dry       │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Required Chemical Formulations & Operating Parameters

* **BOE 6:1 Primary Etchant**:
  * **Composition**: $6\text{ parts } 40\% \text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 1\text{ part } 49\% \text{ HF}$.
  * **pH Target**: $\sim 4.5$ (buffered by $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to maintain constant fluoride ion activity).
  * **Operating Bath Temperature**: $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
* **Surfactant / Wetting Spike**:
  * **Additive**: $0.1\% \text{ v/v}$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad.
  * **Function**: Lowers surface tension to suppress micro-bubble entrapment within high-aspect-ratio oxide contact windows and micro-trenches.
* **Pre-requisite Surface Preparation**:
  * Photoresist pattern primed via HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane) vapor prime at $120^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain resist adhesion and prevent lateral peeling.
* **Cascade Rinse Fluid**:
  * Ultra-Pure Water (UPW), incoming resistivity $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Safety Protocol & PPE Verification**:
   * Don full acid gear: chemical apron, sleeve guards, face shield, and heavy neoprene/nitrile over-gloves.
   * Verify that **Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%)** is unexpired and positioned immediately adjacent to the wet bench.
2. **Etch Bath Conditioning**:
   * In a dedicated fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) tank, verify BOE 6:1 solution is stabilized at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
   * Verify $0.1\%$ wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) is fully dispersed without surface foam.
3. **Immersion Dip-Etch**:
   * Load HMDS-primed and patterned wafer cassette into the PTFE dipper arm.
   * Submerge into BOE 6:1 bath with gentle vertical reciprocal agitation.
   * **Etch Time Calculation**:
     * For **Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch rate is $80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
     * For **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch rate is $150\text{ to } 220\text{ nm/min}$.
     * For **Native oxide clearing**: Etch duration is $10\text{ to } 15\text{ seconds}$.
4. **Cascade Dump Rinse Transfer**:
   * Quickly transfer cassette into the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank within $<3\text{ seconds}$ to avoid air-drying or uncontrolled bevel etching.
   * Execute **5 complete dump-and-fill cycles** with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW.
   * Continue cascade overflow until effluent bath resistivity reads $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
5. **Drying & Hydrophobic Surface Check**:
   * Spin rinse dry (SRD) or pull wafer slowly for observation: bare silicon contact surfaces must display complete hydrophobic water-sheeting/dewetting.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | $80 - 100\text{ nm/min}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Film Thickness Metrology |
| **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $185\text{ nm/min}$ | $150 - 220\text{ nm/min}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry |
| **Cascade Rinse Bath Resistivity** | $> 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-situ Inline UPW Resistivity Sensor (Cell Constant $k=0.01$) |
| **Etch Selectivity ($\text{SiO}_2$ : Si)** | $> 100 : 1$ | Minimum $100:1$ | Cross-sectional Profilometry / Step Height Analysis |

---

### 5. Context Citations

* **[Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)]**:
  * 6:1 formulation ratio ($6\text{ parts } 40\% \text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 1\text{ part } 49\% \text{ HF}$).
  * Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate at $25^\circ\text{C}$ ($\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ / $1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  * Addition of $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 / Fluorad wetting agent for trench bubble elimination.
  * HMDS vapor prime pre-treatment at $120^\circ\text{C}$.
  * Mandatory Calcium Gluconate safety protocol for HF exposure.
* **[Source: Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates]**:
  * Etch rates at $25^\circ\text{C}$: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ ($80 - 100\text{ nm/min}$), CVD/TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ ($150 - 220\text{ nm/min}$), and Native oxide ($10 - 15\text{ s}$).
  * Selectivity ratios: $\text{SiO}_2:\text{Si} > 100:1$; $\text{SiO}_2:\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 > 20:1$.
  * Buffering chemistry maintaining $\text{pH} \sim 4.5$ and constant fluoride ion activity.
* **[Source: RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering]**:
  * Cascade dump rinse protocol: 5 dump cycles using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW.
  * Effluent resistivity endpoint threshold ($> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
  * Hydrophobic surface dewetting endpoint indicator for exposed silicon oxide strip completion.

Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates (Williams, K. - Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems (JMEMS))

```text
│        Fluorad         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Submerged PVDF/PTFE   │
│    Recirculation &     │
│        Wetting         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        Thermal         │
│    Stabilization to    │
│         25.0 °C        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Verification:      │
│   Temperature, Etch    │
│   Rate, Bubble-Free    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Safety & Environment Preparation**:
   - Verify that **calcium gluconate gel** is unexpired, readily accessible, and present at the wet bench station before handling any fluoride chemistries.
   - Don full HF-rated PPE (acid-resistant neoprene/nitrile apron, sleeves, face shield, and chemical-resistant gloves).
2. **Volumetric Reagent Metering & Bath Formulation**:
   - In a clean, dedicated fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) etch tank, dispense **6 parts 40% Ammonium Fluoride ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$)**.
   - Slowly meter in **1 part 49% Hydrofluoric Acid ($\text{HF}$)** under controlled chemical bench exhaust.
   - *Rationale*: Buffered chemistry maintains constant pH, uniform etch rates, and prevents rapid depletion of free HF.
3. **Surfactant Spiking (Wetting Agent Addition)**:
   - Add **0.1% by volume** of wetting agent (**Triton X-100** or **Fluorad**) into the formulated BOE 6:1 mixture.
   - Gently stir with a PTFE paddle or engage low-shear bath recirculation to homogeneously disperse the surfactant without introducing froth.
   - *Rationale*: Eliminates surface tension barriers and bubble entrapment in high-aspect-ratio patterns and micro-trenches.
4. **Circulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Engage the inline temperature-controlled recirculation loop (fluoropolymer heat exchanger/chiller).
   - Set the bath temperature controller to **25.0 °C**.
   - Maintain recirculation until the inline temperature probe reads steady-state equilibrium at 25.0 °C.
5. **Pre-Run Pilot Verification**:
   - Measure bath temperature via calibrated inline RTD/thermocouple.
   - Perform a qualification dip using a bare thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ monitor wafer to verify nominal etch rate prior to releasing the bath for production lot processing.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Formulation Ratio** | 6 : 1 ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ 40% : $\text{HF}$ 49%) | Volumetric ratio | Automated chemical metering / titrator |
| **Surfactant Concentration** | $0.1\%$ | $\text{vol}\%$ (or $\text{wt}\%$) | Precision analytical dispense / micropipette |
| **Stabilized Bath Temperature** | $25.0 \pm 0.5$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Calibrated inline PTFE-sheathed RTD / thermocouple |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $\approx 100 \pm 5$ ($1000 \pm 50$) | $\text{nm/min}$ ($\text{Å/min}$) | Spectroscopic ellipsometry / reflectometry on monitor wafer |
| **Bubble Entrapment / Micro-trench Wetting** | $0$ entrapped micro-bubbles | Count / defects per unit area | Post-etch optical/defect inspection |

---

### Context Citations
- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - Formulated as 6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$.
  - Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at 25 °C is approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - Constant pH buffer avoids rapid $\text{HF}$ depletion.
  - Wetting agent addition ($0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad) eliminates bubble entrapment in micro-trenches.
  - HF calcium binding hazard requiring calcium gluconate gel presence at all times.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Info
- **Title**: BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration
- **Action Type**: Make
- **Generation**: Gen 1 (mm / 180nm Planar DRAM Node)
- **Hierarchy Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse > Surfactant-Spiked BOE 6:1 Bath Formulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization > BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration

---

## 1. Safety & PPE Protocols
> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) Hazard:** HF penetrates skin deeply without immediate burn sensation and binds with systemic serum calcium ($Ca^{2+}$) and magnesium ($Mg^{2+}$), causing severe hypocalcemia, cardiac arrest, and tissue necrosis.
- Inspect the wet bench safety station: Ensure unexpired **Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%)** is physically present and accessible within reach at the wet bench before opening chemical containers.
- Required PPE: Chemically resistant fluoropolymer/neoprene apron, heavy-duty Viton/neoprene gauntlets over nitrile inner gloves, chemical splash face shield, and chemical safety goggles.
- Perform all operations inside a certified laminar downflow wet bench with exhausted polypropylene/PVDF deck and acid vapor scrubbers active.

---

## 2. Chemical Formulation & Compounding Sequence

### 2.1 Formulation Ratio
- **Stock Chemistry:**
  - 6 volume parts of $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ (Ammonium Fluoride, electronic grade).
  - 1 volume part of $49\%\ \text{HF}$ (Hydrofluoric Acid, electronic grade).
- **Buffering & pH Action:** Maintains constant fluoride ion activity and bath $\text{pH} \approx 4.5$, preventing rapid HF depletion during high-throughput oxide etching.
- **Surfactant Dosing:** $0.1\%\ (\text{v/v})$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad wetting agent to lower surface tension and eliminate micro-trench air bubble entrapment.

### 2.2 Compounding Steps
1. **PVDF/Teflon Tank Inspection:** Confirm the constant-temperature recirculation bath and PTFE immersion heater/chiller coils are thoroughly pre-cleaned and free of foreign particulate matter.
2. **Ammonium Fluoride Addition:** Dispense 6 parts by volume of $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ into the fluoropolymer bath tank.
3. **Hydrofluoric Acid Addition:** Slowly add 1 part by volume of $49\%\ \text{HF}$ into the $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ solution under continuous magnetic/recirculation pump agitation.
   > [!WARNING]
   > Always add acid into the buffered ammonium fluoride base, never reverse, to avoid localized thermal spikes.
4. **Surfactant Wetting Dosing:** Accurately meter and dispense $0.1\%\ (\text{v/v})$ of Triton X-100 (or Fluorad) directly into the agitated bulk BOE solution.
5. **Homogenization:** Maintain internal recirculation at low shear for 15 minutes to guarantee homogeneous surfactant micelle distribution without excessive frothing.

---

## 3. Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration & Thermal Stabilization

1. **Setpoint Calibration:** Power on the fluoropolymer recirculating immersion bath controller and establish the setpoint temperature at **$25.0^\circ\text{C}$**.
2. **Thermal Stabilization:** Allow the recirculating fluid loop to stabilize until external calibrated RTD/PT100 immersion probes read $25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ steadily across all quadrants of the bath.
3. **Etch Rate Verification (Dummy Monitor Wafer):**
   - Take a clean pilot monitor wafer with thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ pre-measured via spectroscopic ellipsometry.
   - Perform a calibrated test dip-etch in the stabilized $25^\circ\text{C}$ BOE 6:1 bath.
   - Verify the baseline thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate aligns within $80\ \text{nm/min}$ to $100\ \text{nm/min}$ ($800\ \text{to}\ 1000\ \text{\AA/min}$).

---

## 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Tolerance | Units | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Volumetric Compounding Ratio** | $6 : 1$ ($40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F} : 49\%\ \text{HF}$) | $\pm 0.5\%$ | Ratio ($\text{v/v}$) | Automated In-line Chemical Dispense Flowmeters |
| **Surfactant Concentration** | $0.1$ | $\pm 0.01$ | $\%\ (\text{v/v})$ | Precision Metered Dosing Pump Calibration |
| **Bath Operating Temperature** | $25.0$ | $\pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion RTD / Teflon-sheathed PT100 Sensor |
| **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $80.0\ \text{to}\ 100.0$ ($800\ \text{to}\ 1000$) | Within range | $\text{nm/min}$ ($\text{\AA/min}$) | Pre/Post Spectroscopic Ellipsometry at $25^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **Solution Equilibrium pH** | $4.5$ | $\pm 0.2$ | $\text{pH}$ | HF-Resistant In-line Fluoropolymer pH Electrode |

---

## 5. Literature References Context
- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**: Confirms formulation (6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F} : 1$ part $49\%\ \text{HF}$), thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate of $\sim 100\ \text{nm/min}$ ($1000\ \text{\AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$, surfactant dosing ($0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to prevent bubble entrapment, and mandatory calcium gluconate gel protocols.
- **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates**: Confirms buffering chemistry mechanism ($\text{pH} \sim 4.5$, constant fluoride ion activity), thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ rate range ($80\ \text{to}\ 100\ \text{nm/min}$ / $800\ \text{to}\ 1000\ \text{\AA/min}$), and CVD/TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ rates ($150\ \text{to}\ 220\ \text{nm/min}$).
citations: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE) (Semiconductor Chemical Processing Handbook)
Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates (Williams, K. - Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems (JMEMS))
RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering (Kern, W. - Handbook of Semiconductor Wafer Cleaning Technology)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title:** BOE 6:1 Stoichiometric Compounding & 0.1% Wetting Surfactant Dosing
- **Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > [Architecture & Integration] > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning [Chemical Processing] > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution [Wet Chemistry] > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse [Wet Chemistry] > Surfactant-Spiked BOE 6:1 Bath Formulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization [Wet Chemistry] > BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration [Wet Chemistry] > BOE 6:1 Stoichiometric Compounding & 0.1% Wetting Surfactant Dosing [Wet Chemistry]
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Buy / Formulate

---

## 1. Safety & PPE Pre-Requisites
> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid Hazard**: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) penetrates skin and deeply binds systemic calcium. An unexpired tube of **calcium gluconate gel** must be present within arm's reach at the wet bench before opening chemical containers. Operators must wear full acid-gear: fluoropolymer apron, heavy neoprene/Viton over-gloves, and a face shield.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|             BOE 6:1 COMPOUNDING & SURFACTANT DOSING FLOW                     |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  [Step 1: Prep & Tare]           Clean fluoropolymer PVDF/PTFE vessel
         │
         ▼
  [Step 2: NH4F Addition]         Dispense 6 volumetric parts 40% NH4F
         │
         ▼
  [Step 3: HF Addition]           Dispense 1 volumetric part 49% HF into NH4F
         │
         ▼
  [Step 4: Surfactant Dosing]     Pipette 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 or Fluorad
         │
         ▼
  [Step 5: Homogenization]        PTFE impeller stir; equilibrate to 25°C
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Labware Preparation and Safety Check
1. Ensure the dedicated laminar flow wet bench exhaust velocity is nominal.
2. Verify calcium gluconate gel availability and expiry.
3. Clean and inspect a dedicated acid-compatible fluoropolymer (PTFE/PVDF or PFA) mixing container; verify zero particulate contamination.

### Step 2: Volumetric Dispensing of Buffer (40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$)
1. Measure exactly **6 volumetric parts** of semiconductor-grade **40% Ammonium Fluoride ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$)** solution (e.g., 600 mL).
2. Pour the measured $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ into the PTFE compounding vessel.

### Step 3: Stoichiometric Hydrofluoric Acid (49% HF) Addition
1. Measure exactly **1 volumetric part** of semiconductor-grade **49% Hydrofluoric Acid ($\text{HF}$)** solution (e.g., 100 mL).
2. Slowly decant the $49\%\ \text{HF}$ into the $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ solution under laminar exhaust to prevent local heating and splattering. Maintain the 6:1 volumetric ratio to buffer against HF depletion and lock bath pH.

### Step 4: Surfactant Dosing (0.1% Wetting Agent)
1. Using an acid-resistant micropipette, draw **0.1% by volume** of wetting surfactant (**Triton X-100** or **Fluorad**) (e.g., 0.70 mL for a 700 mL total compounding batch).
2. Dispense the wetting agent directly into the center of the liquid column to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment and lower surface tension.

### Step 5: Homogenization and Thermal Stabilization
1. Stir the solution using a high-purity PTFE magnetic stir bar or PTFE paddle for 3–5 minutes until the surfactant is completely dissolved without foaming.
2. Cover the bath with a fluoropolymer vapor-containment lid and allow the temperature to stabilize at **25°C** prior to wafer qualification.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Range | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stoichiometric Volume Ratio** | **6:1** ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : $\text{HF}$) | $\pm 0.5\%$ by volume | Calibrated PFA graduated cylinder / mass balance |
| **Surfactant Concentration** | **0.1%** | $\pm 0.01\%$ v/v | Precision acid micropipette |
| **Bath Calibration Temperature** | **25°C** | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion fluoropolymer-sheathed PT100 RTD |
| **SiO₂ Etch Rate Baseline** | **100 nm/min** (1000 Å/min) | $\pm 5\%$ at 25°C | Pre/post spectroscopic ellipsometry on thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ test wafer |

---

  - Stoichiometry: *6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$*.
  - Etch rate: *Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at 25°C is approximately 100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min)*.
  - Wetting agent: *0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad added to eliminate bubble entrapment in micro-trenches*.
  - Safety protocol: *Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present at all times*.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-MET-004`
**Title:** Recirculating Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration & Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch-Rate Metrology  
**Node Path:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Architecture & Integration > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse > Surfactant-Spiked BOE 6:1 Bath Formulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization > BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration > Recirculating Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration & Thermal SiO2 Etch-Rate Metrology`  
**Generation:** Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Safety Protocol:** HF Emergency Protocol Active (Ensure Calcium Gluconate Gel is accessible and unexpired).

---

### 1. Process Overview & Calibration Setup

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Recirculation & Thermal Equilibration (25.0°C)          |
|    - Pump Rate: Recirculating PVDF/PTFE Bath                 |
|    - Temperature Target: 25.0°C (Stable within ±0.5°C)      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Pre-Etch Ellipsometry Baseline                           |
|    - Measure initial thermal SiO2 film thickness (T1)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Timed Calibration Dip-Etch                               |
|    - 6:1 BOE (6 parts 40% NH4F : 1 part 49% HF)             |
|    - Surfactant: 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad               |
|    - Duration: Exactly 60.0 seconds immersion               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Quick Dump Rinse (QDR), Spin Dry & Post-Etch Metrology   |
|    - Measure remaining thermal SiO2 thickness (T2)          |
|    - Calculate Etch Rate: (T1 - T2) / 1.0 min               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **PPE & Workstation Verification:**
   - Don full acid PPE: chemical apron, heavy neoprene gloves, face shield, and chemical vapor respirator.
   - Verify the immediate presence of unexpired **Calcium Gluconate Gel** at the chemical wet bench.

2. **Constant-Temperature Recirculation Stabilization:**
   - Fill the recirculating chemical-duty bath with compounded **BOE 6:1** formulation (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$) spiked with **0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad** wetting agent.
   - Engage the recirculation loop to purge trapped micro-bubbles and achieve homogeneous mixture.
   - Set the bath temperature controller to **25.0°C**. Allow bath to recirculate until thermal equilibrium is attained and stabilizes within target tolerances.

3. **Pre-Etch Thickness Metrology:**
   - Load a clean monitor test wafer with a known thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ layer into the spectroscopic ellipsometer/reflectometer.
   - Map a 5-point thickness profile across the wafer surface and record average baseline thickness $T_1$ in nm (or Å).

4. **Calibration Immersion Etch:**
   - Transfer the monitor wafer using a PTFE carrier boat into the 25.0°C recirculating BOE 6:1 bath.
   - Immerse the wafer and agitate gently for exactly **60.0 seconds** (1.00 minute) under constant recirculation.

5. **Cascade Rinse & Decontamination:**
   - Immediately withdraw the wafer carrier and transfer directly into the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank filled with deionized (DI) water to halt the etching reaction.
   - Run three consecutive dump cycles, followed by cascade overflow rinsing until resistivity reaches $> 18\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Transfer to the spin rinse dryer (SRD) and cycle with warm filtered $\text{N}_2$.

6. **Post-Etch Metrology & Rate Computation:**
   - Measure the remaining oxide thickness $T_2$ across the same 5 measurement locations.
   - Calculate the etch rate:
     $$\text{Etch Rate} = \frac{T_1 - T_2}{1.0\ \text{min}}\ (\text{nm/min})$$
   - Confirm calculated rate aligns with baseline qualification values before releasing the bath to production wafer lots.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Recirculating Bath Temperature** | 25.0 | $\pm 0.5$ | °C | Calibrated In-situ Thermocouple / RTD Probe |
| **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | 100.0 | $\pm 5.0$ (approx. 1000 Å/min) | nm/min | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry |
| **Wetting Agent Dosing** | 0.1 | Nominal | % vol/vol | Volumetric Dispense Sensor / Recipe Log |
| **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Hard Mask Selectivity Loss Rate** | $< 0.5$ | Maximum allowable | nm/min | Comparative Ellipsometry Calibration |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources Cited

1. **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**
   - *Composition & Chemistry:* BOE 6:1 formulated with 6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ and 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$.
   - *Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate:* Approximately $100\ \text{nm/min}$ ($1000\ \text{\AA/min}$) at 25°C.
   - *Additives & Adhesion:* Inclusion of $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad surfactant prevents bubble entrapment in micro-trenches; HMDS vapor prime executed at 120°C prior to resist coating.
   - *Safety Critical:* Mandatory continuous presence of calcium gluconate gel for HF exposure mitigation.
2. **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
   - *Etch Mask Resistance:* Verified $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ etch rate $< 0.5\ \text{nm/min}$ in BOE.
3. **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
   - *PID Thermal Tolerance Standards:* Temperature uniformity targets established to maintain thermal control within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks (Kern & Rosler - Chemically Vapor Deposited Synthetic Materials)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** `SOP-WET-MET-004`  
**Classification:** Gen 1 (mm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip Architecture & Integration  
**Unit Process:** Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning  
**Task Title:** Thermal Stabilization Profiling, Contact Angle Surface Tension Metrology & Baseline Etch Rate Qualification

---

## 1. Process Workflow Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│       Formulate       │
│   Surfactant-Spiked   │
│     BOE 6:1 Bath      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│        Thermal        │
│     Stabilization     │
│   Profiling at 25.0°C │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Contact Angle &    │
│    Surface Tension    │
│       Metrology       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Baseline Etch Rate   │
│   Qualification on    │
│     Thermal SiO2      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────◇───────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria  │
│        Passed?        │
└─────┬───────────┬─────┘
   Yes│           │No
      ▼           ▼
┌───────────┐ ┌───────────────┐
│  Release  │ │ Quarantine &  │
│   Bath    │ │  Re-profile   │
└───────────┘ └───────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Safety & PPE Protocols

> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) Contact Hazard:**
> HF penetrates skin deeply without immediate sensation of pain, dissociates, and chelates systemic calcium ions ($Ca^{2+}$).
> - **Mandatory PPE:** Acid-rated apron, full face shield, heavy neoprene/PVDF gloves over nitrile inner gloves.
> - **Emergency Response:** An unexpired tube of **calcium gluconate gel** must be present within arm's reach of the wet bench at all times prior to opening the chemical bath enclosure.

---

## 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Step 1: Chemical Bath Formulation & Wetting Verification
1. Ensure the bath vessel contains standard **BOE 6:1** formulated from:
   - **6 parts** $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ (Ammonium Fluoride)
   - **1 part** $49\%\ \text{HF}$ (Hydrofluoric Acid)
2. Verify the surfactant additive concentration:
   - Wetting agent: **$0.1\%$ Triton X-100** (or Fluorad) by volume to eliminate bubble entrapment in micro-trenches.
3. Verify bath pH stabilizes at $\mathbf{\sim 4.5}$ via constant fluoride ion activity.

### Step 2: Thermal Stabilization Profiling
1. Activate the recirculating immersion chiller/heater bath loop with inert PTFE/PVDF plumbing.
2. Monitor bath temperature using an acid-encapsulated RTD probe.
3. Profile and hold bath temperature at **$25^\circ\text{C}$** until thermal equilibrium is maintained within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across the tank profile for $\ge 30\text{ minutes}$.

### Step 3: Surface Tension & Contact Angle Metrology
1. Extract a $5.0\text{ mL}$ aliquot sample from the stabilized bath.
2. Load an HMDS-primed wafer test coupon ($120^\circ\text{C}$ vapor prime) into the automated optical goniometer.
3. Dispense a $5\ \mu\text{L}$ sessile droplet of the surfactant-spiked BOE solution onto the coupon.
4. Record baseline contact angle $\theta$ and verify rapid surface wetting with zero micro-bubble entrapment across the liquid-wafer interface.

### Step 4: Baseline Etch Rate Qualification Run
1. Select a prime monitor wafer with **thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$** (dry or wet oxide).
2. Measure initial oxide thickness ($T_0$) at 9 or 13 points using an optical ellipsometer/reflectometer ($n \approx 1.46$).
3. Immerse the test wafer into the $25^\circ\text{C}$ BOE 6:1 bath with gentle vertical agitation for a timed cycle of exactly **$60\text{ seconds}$** ($1.00\text{ min}$).
4. Immediately transfer into the dump rinser / cascade overflow rinse bath for a minimum $>5\text{-cycle}$ DI water rinse until effluent resistivity exceeds $18\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$; spin-rinse-dry with filtered $\text{N}_2$.
5. Measure post-etch thickness ($T_1$) at the identical 9 or 13 points. Calculate the average etch rate:
   $$\text{Etch Rate} = \frac{T_0 - T_1}{1.0\ \text{min}}$$

---

## 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method / Tooling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bath Temperature** | **$25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** | Inline PTFE-sheathed RTD temperature sensor |
| **Bath pH** | **$\text{pH } 4.5 \pm 0.2$** | Fluoride-resistant immersion pH probe |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | **$80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$** ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (pre/post-etch delta at $25^\circ\text{C}$) |
| **Etch Selectivity ($\text{SiO}_2 : \text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$)** | **$> 20 : 1$** ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 \text{ etch rate} < 0.5\text{ nm/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry on LPCVD $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ coupon ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$) |

---

## 5. Source Citations & References

- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - Formulation ratio: 6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part $49\%\ \text{HF}$.
  - Etch rate of thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C} \approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - Surfactant wetting spike: $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad.
  - HMDS vapor prime pre-treatment condition: $120^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Safety requirement: Immediate availability of calcium gluconate gel.
- **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates:**
  - Buffering mechanism: $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ stabilizes fluoride ion activity and maintains solution $\text{pH } \sim 4.5$.
  - Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate window: $80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Etch selectivity: $\text{SiO}_2 : \text{single-crystal Si} > 100:1$; $\text{SiO}_2 : \text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 > 20:1$.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:**
  - LPCVD $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ baseline characteristics ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$).
  - Chemical resistance to BOE: Etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$.
citations: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE) (Semiconductor Chemical Processing Handbook)
Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates (Williams, K. - Journal of Microelectromechanical Systems (JMEMS))
Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks (Kern & Rosler - Chemically Vapor Deposited Synthetic Materials)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Equilibrium Profiling & Recirculating Bath Temperature Mapping

**Scope:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — Wet Chemical Processing Station  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Safety Caution:** Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present and inspected at the station at all times prior to operating the bath.

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Fill Bath with BOE   │
│   6:1 & 0.1% Wetting   │
│         Agent          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        Initiate        │
│    Recirculation &     │
│      Heating Loop      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Deploy 5-Point PFA   │
│   Thermocouple Array   │◄─╮
└────────────┬───────────┘  │
             │              │
             ▼              │
┌────────────────────────┐  │
│     Log Real-Time      │  │
│    Thermal Gradient    │  │
│        Mapping         │  │
└────────────┬───────────┘  │
             │              │
             ▼              │
┌────────────◇───────────┐  │
│   Stable at 25.0°C ±   │  │
│         0.5°C?         │  │
└────────────◇───────────┘  │
             │              │
           No├──────────────┼──────────────╮Yes
             ▼              │              ▼
┌────────────────────────┐  │ ┌────────────────────────┐
│   Tune Recirculation   │  │ │  Qualify Bath Thermal  │
│        PID Loop        ├──╯ │      Equilibrium       │
└────────────────────────┘    └────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Safety & Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Inspection**
   - Confirm availability and expiration of topically applied calcium gluconate antidote gel at the chemical wet bench.
   - Don acid-resistant gear: heavy neoprene/nitrile sleeves, chemical apron, face shield, and gauntlet gloves.

2. **Chemical Bath Charging & Wetting Agent Spiking**
   - Charge the recirculating fluoropolymer (PVDF/PFA) bath with standard BOE 6:1 solution (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$).
   - Spike the mixture with 0.1% wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to suppress micro-trench bubble entrapment and establish consistent surface wetting.

3. **Recirculation & Temperature Controller Activation**
   - Start the magnetic-drive chemical circulation pump to maintain steady chemical turnover through the inline filter.
   - Power on the bath immersion heat exchanger / recirculating chiller loop and program the digital PID controller setpoint to **25.0°C**.

4. **Multi-Point Temperature Sensor Grid Mapping**
   - Immerse a qualified 5-point PFA-encapsulated thermocouple profiling array into the active wafer immersion zone (measuring center, front, back, left, and right spatial locations).
   - Log multi-channel temperature data at 10-second intervals for a continuous 20-minute stabilization window.

5. **Thermal Equilibrium Mapping & PID Tuning**
   - Map spatial temperature variations across the active wafer cassette zone to verify elimination of localized convection dead spots.
   - Adjust PID loop proportional gain ($P$) and integral time ($I$) as necessary until the maximum delta between any two mapping nodes satisfies stability criteria.

6. **Equilibrium Sign-Off & Release for Etch Qualification**
   - Record spatial delta values and average steady-state temperature into the run log sheet.
   - Proceed to baseline oxide etch rate qualification.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Tolerance | Verified Context Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Steady-State Bath Temperature** | `25.0` | `±0.5` | `°C` |
| **Spatial Bath Temperature Uniformity** | `≤ 0.5` | Max across 300 mm cassette envelope | `°C` |
| **Wetting Agent Spiking Concentration** | `0.1` | `±0.01` | `% (vol/vol)` |
| **Baseline Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | `100` (equivalent to `1000 Å/min`) | `±5` | `nm/minute` |

---

### Context Citations

- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - BOE 6:1 composition (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$).
  - Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ nominal etch rate baseline: 100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min) at 25°C.
  - Wetting agent addition: 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment.
  - Mandatory safety protocol: Calcium gluconate gel presence due to HF calcium-binding hazard.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - Closed-loop PID temperature uniformity tolerance of $\pm 0.5\text{°C}$ across processing regions.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Surfactant Dynamic Surface Tension & Contact Angle Goniometry Metrology

**Task Title:** Surfactant Dynamic Surface Tension & Contact Angle Goniometry Metrology  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch & Patterning Qualification  
**Equipment / Action Type:** Buy / Metrology End-Station (Optical Contact Angle Goniometer & Maximum Bubble Pressure Tensiometer)

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sample Spiked Bath   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Dynamic Tensiometry  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Contact Angle     │
│       Metrology       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Wet Etch Release    │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Safety Protocol & Environmental Setup:**
   - Verify HF safety readiness inside the chemical exhaust hood. Confirm the immediate availability of calcium gluconate gel before handling fluorinated reagents or BOE aliquots.
   - Maintain the metrology thermal stage and cleanroom ambient temperature strictly at **25°C**.
2. **Bath Sampling & Dynamic Surface Tension Qualification:**
   - Draw a 20 mL aliquot from the freshly stabilized BOE (6:1 NH₄F:HF) bath formulated with **0.1% Triton X-100 (or Fluorad)** wetting agent.
   - Insert the capillary probe of the calibrated Maximum Bubble Pressure Tensiometer into the chemical aliquot.
   - Measure dynamic surface tension across surface age intervals (10 ms to 10,000 ms) to verify dynamic surfactant diffusion kinetics required to prevent bubble entrapment in high-aspect-ratio micro-trenches (such as 180nm DRAM capacitor contact openings).
3. **Substrate Preparation & Goniometric Sessile Drop Dispense:**
   - Prepare a monitor wafer coupon matching the targeted interface: HMDS-primed (vapor primed at **120°C**) Shipley 1813 resist-patterned substrate over thermal SiO₂.
   - Mount the coupon on the motorized stage of the optical contact angle goniometer.
   - Dispense a calibrated sessile droplet (2–5 µL) of the surfactant-spiked BOE solution onto the patterned resist surface and oxide test pads via automated micro-syringe.
4. **Image Acquisition & Baseline Qualification:**
   - Capture high-resolution droplet profiles at 0.1 s, 1.0 s, and 5.0 s post-dispense using the telecentric camera system.
   - Apply the Young-Laplace fitting algorithm to determine advancing, receding, and equilibrium contact angles ($\theta$).
   - Confirm complete wetting and absence of pinned micro-bubbles at trench sidewalls prior to clearing the wet dip-etch line.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                     Baseline Process Target Values     
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░░░░░░                               │
    PR Uniformity┤░░░░░░                               │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   SiO2 Etch Rate┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   Etch Bath Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
Triton X-100 Conc┤█                                    │
                 │█                                    │
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                  0       25       50       75      100 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance / Range | Measurement Unit | Qualification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Wetting Agent Spiking Concentration** | `0.1` | $\pm 0.01$ | `%` (vol/vol) | High-precision micro-dispenser / formulation assay |
| **Bath & Metrology Temperature** | `25` | $\pm 0.5$ | `°C` | In-situ calibrated RTD thermal probe |
| **Thermally Grown SiO₂ Etch Rate Baseline** | `100` (`1000`) | $\pm 5$ ($\pm 50$) | `nm/min` (`Å/min`) | Spectroscopic ellipsometry pre/post dip-etch |
| **Resist Film Thickness & Cross-Wafer Uniformity** | `1.30` | $\pm 0.015$ ($\pm 15$ nm) | `µm` | Optical film thickness reflectometry (100mm wafer) |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Reference Context

- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - Chemical formulation: 6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$.
  - Etch rate standard: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at **25°C** is approximately **100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min)**.
  - Wetting agent addition: **0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad** added to eliminate bubble entrapment in micro-trenches and preserve constant pH and uniform etch rates.
  - Safety mandate: Hydrofluoric acid binds calcium upon skin penetration; calcium gluconate gel must remain present at all times.
- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming:**
  - Surface modification: HMDS vapor prime at **120°C** reactively silylates hydrophilic silanol ($-\text{Si}-\text{OH}$) groups to prevent photoresist lift-off during BOE acid wet etching.
  - Coating baseline: Shipley 1813 spin recipe yields **1.30 µm ± 15 nm** film across 100mm substrates.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology (Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench):**
  - Structural context: $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ folded bitline access geometry with channel dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, requiring wetting into deep contact openings without micro-bubble pinning.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-BOE-001
**Title:** Ellipsometric Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Baseline Etch Rate & Uniformity Qualification  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 2 µm)  
**Safety Protocol:** Hydrofluoric acid binds calcium and penetrates dermal tissue. Certified HF PPE (neoprene apron/gloves, face shield) and Calcium Gluconate gel must be on-station prior to bath approach.

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Pre-Etch        │
│     Spectroscopic      │
│      Ellipsometry      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Bath Thermal      │
│    Stabilization at    │
│          25°C          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Surfactant-Spike BOE  │
│     6:1 Timed Dip      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    DI Water Cascade    │
│     Overflow Rinse     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Post-Etch        │
│     Ellipsometry &     │
│     Uniformity Map     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Etch Ellipsometry Baseline Mapping:**
   - Load clean baseline thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ pilot monitor wafer into spectroscopic ellipsometer stage.
   - Execute multi-point radial scan (film refractive index baseline $n \approx 1.46$). Record mean starting oxide thickness ($T_0$) across the wafer.

2. **Wet Station Thermal & Chemical Verification:**
   - Verify the recirculating constant-temperature fluoropolymer bath of BOE 6:1 (6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part $49\%\ \text{HF}$) spiked with $0.1\%$ Triton X-100/Fluorad wetting agent.
   - Confirm calibrated bath thermocouple reads steady-state at $25.0^\circ\text{C}$.

3. **Timed Dip-Etch Execution:**
   - Mount monitor wafer into PTFE wafer cassette.
   - Submerge wafer into surfactant-spiked BOE bath for exactly $60.0\text{ s}$ under mild vertical agitation to eliminate bubble entrapment.

4. **Quench & Cascade DI Rinse:**
   - Transfer cassette immediately (< 3 s dry transfer) into high-resistivity DI water cascade overflow tank.
   - Rinse for $\ge 5\text{ min}$ until bath effluent reaches resistivity $> 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$, followed by spin-rinse dry (SRD) with filtered $\text{N}_2$.

5. **Post-Etch Ellipsometric Measurement & Calculation:**
   - Remeasure remaining oxide thickness ($T_1$) at the identical coordinate sites on the spectroscopic ellipsometer.
   - Calculate etch rate ($\text{ER} = \frac{T_0 - T_1}{t}$) and full-wafer within-wafer non-uniformity ($\text{WIWNU} = \frac{T_{\max} - T_{\min}}{2 \times T_{\text{mean}}} \times 100\%$).

---

### Baseline Etch Comparison

```text
                  BOE 6:1 Baseline Etch Rate (nm/min)   
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │░                                      │
Si3N4 Hard Mask┤░                                      │
   Thermal SiO2┤███████████████████████████████████████│
               │███████████████████████████████████████│
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
                0        25       50        75      100 
```

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Operational / Physical Metric | Acceptance Range | Monitoring Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bath Temperature** | Steady-state operating temperature | $25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated bath thermocouple / RTD probe |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | Rate of oxide removal | $100\text{ nm/min} \pm 5\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min} \pm 50\text{ \AA/min}$) | Multi-point Spectroscopic Ellipsometer |
| **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Etch Selectivity Guard** | Etch resistance of LPCVD nitride | $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ (Selectivity $> 200:1$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$) |
| **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity** | Thickness variation across diameter | $\le 1.5\%$ ($1\sigma$) | Multi-point Ellipsometric radial map |

---

### Context Citations

- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - Chemical composition: 6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part $49\%\ \text{HF}$.
  - Baseline etch rate: $\approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) for thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Wetting agent: $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad added for bubble elimination in micro-trenches.
  - Safety requirement: Continuous presence of calcium gluconate gel for dermal HF neutralization.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:**
  - $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ refractive index: $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$.
  - Nitride etch barrier: Highly resistant to BOE with etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Timed Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution with Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Rinse

**Document ID:** `SOP-WET-180NM-BOE-002`  
**Classification:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Wafer Prep & HMDS   │
│         120C         │
│                      │
```
