# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: PTFE Wet Bench Procurement & Acid Exhaust Ducting Integration
**Module:** Wet Chemistry / Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup  
**Technology Node Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### Process Execution Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  PTFE Bench Receiving  │
│        and Spec        │
│      Verification      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acid Exhaust Ducting  │
│       and Flange       │
│      Interfacing       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Magnehelic       │
│      Differential      │
│   Pressure and Face    │
│   Velocity Balancing   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  DI Water Quick Dump   │
│   Rinse and Drainage   │
│      Flow Checks       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Substrate Wet Clean   │
│        and Etch        │
│     Commissioning      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Procurement & Material Verification:**
   - Procure and receive a semiconductor-grade, seamless-welded virgin Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) wet chemical bench equipped with segregated baths (HF/BOE native oxide stripping bath, SC-1/SC-2 RCA stations, and integrated Quick Dump Rinse [QDR] cascade tanks).
   - Inspect internal chemical supply lines (PFA/PTFE tubing), pneumatic acid-rated dump valves, and high-impact transparent chemical sash guards.

2. **Ducting & Flange Interfacing:**
   - Couple the wet bench acid exhaust collar to the sub-fab centralized acid scrubber lateral line using corrosion-proof, flame-retardant polypropylene (FRPP) or fluoropolymer-lined stainless steel ducting.
   - Install airtight EPDM/PTFE-encapsulated flange gaskets and torqued stainless steel band clamps along all duct joints.
   - Integrate an adjustable blast gate manual damper and a dedicated differential pressure tap (1/4-inch NPT) ahead of the main exhaust drop.

3. **Exhaust Aerodynamic Balancing & Pressure Verification:**
   - Commission and calibrate a dual-scale Magnehelic differential pressure gauge across the plenum duct connection.
   - Adjust the blast gate to balance negative duct draft until steady-state negative static pressure is achieved.
   - Measure multi-point face capture velocity across the open sash opening using a calibrated hot-wire anemometer to confirm zero chemical fume backflow into the cleanroom aisle.

4. **Safety Interlocks & Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) Drainage Commissioning:**
   - Wire low-exhaust static pressure cutoff interlocks to the master wet bench chemical dispensing solenoids to automatically isolate chemical dispense if exhaust failure occurs.
   - Plumb acid-waste drainage to the dedicated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) collection pipe with double-containment piping.
   - Run ultra-pure DI water through the QDR cycle to verify rapid pneumatic dump timing, leak integrity, and drain clearance without bubbling or back-pressure.

5. **Final Substrate Clean Process Readiness:**
   - Ready the bench for critical 180nm DRAM front-end and back-end wet surface conditioning (such as pre-gate/pre-dielectric native oxide clean before furnace ONO oxidation and pre-metallization deglaze before PVD sputtering).

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
Acceptance Criteria Operating Targets
                         ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                         │░░░░░░                       │
Exhaust Redundancy Margin┤░░░░░░                       │
                         │▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
    QDR Rinse Resistivity┤▒▒▒▒▒▒                       │
    Face Capture Velocity┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
      Duct Static Delta P┤█                            │
                         │█                            │
                         └┬──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0.0   26.2   52.5   78.8 105.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria | Target Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Duct Static Differential Pressure ($\Delta P$)** | **$-1.20 \text{ to } -1.80$** (Target: **$-1.50$**) | $\text{in. w.g.}$ (inches water gauge) / [$\approx -300 \text{ to } -450 \text{ Pa}$] | In-line calibrated Magnehelic gauge / static pressure transducer |
| **Sash Face Capture Velocity** | **$100 \pm 10$** (Minimum: $\ge 90$) | $\text{fpm}$ (feet per minute) / [$\approx 0.51 \pm 0.05 \text{ m/s}$] | 8-point hot-wire anemometer grid at maximum sash working height |
| **QDR DI Water Rinse Resistivity** | **$\ge 18.0$** (Target: **$18.2$**) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated resistivity probe at QDR dump overflow weir |
| **Exhaust Safety Cutoff Threshold** | Static pressure drop below **$-0.50$** initiates auto-shutoff in **$\le 500$** | $\text{in. w.g.} \text{ / } \text{ms}$ | Pneumatic interlock trip simulation via purge damper perturbation |

---

### Citations & Literature Context Integration

1. **Context: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - The wet bench provides critical surface preparation and wafer cleaning for stacked capacitor structures, ensuring zero interfacial contamination for tungsten plug contacts and high-$\kappa$ ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5\text{ / }\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric stacks required to meet the minimum **$28\text{ fF/cell}$** capacitance budget and sub-**$1\text{ fA/cell}$** leakage limit at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Context: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
   - The wet chemical station performs post-etch chemical residue removal and pre-metallization surface preparation prior to planar DC magnetron sputtering of **$\text{Al-0.5\% Cu}$** (350 nm $\pm 5\%$) to maintain low interconnect sheet resistance ($R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$).
3. **Context: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
   - Upstream native oxide stripping and RCA clean in the PTFE wet bench prepare wafers prior to load insertion into the multi-zone quartz furnace (operated at $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ uniformity between $800^\circ\text{C}$ and $1150^\circ\text{C}$ with carrier gas flow regulated at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$) to prevent defect nucleation and crystallographic slip.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects (Vossen & Kern - Thin Film Processes)
Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & $\text{N}_2$ Purge Installation

**Module:** Architecture & Integration > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Wet Chemistry  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 1 mm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Architecture & Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     PFA Chemical      │
│   Distribution Bath   │
│       Plumbing        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sub-Micron UPW Fill  │
│    & Cascade Dump     │
│        Rinser         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Resistivity Sensor   │
│   Monitoring: 18.2    │
│        MOhm-cm        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Point-of-Use 0.05um  │
│   Filtered N2 Purge   │
│        Drying         │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Installation & Commissioning Procedure

#### Step 1: PFA Wet Bench Acid Bath Plumbing Installation
1. Route high-purity Perfluoroalkoxy (PFA) dual-containment tubing with flared PTFE fittings to service the RCA-1 ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 : \text{UPW}$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$), Native Oxide Strip ($1:50\text{ to }1:100\text{ HF} : \text{UPW}$ at $22^\circ\text{C}$), and RCA-2 ($\text{HCl} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 : \text{UPW}$ at $75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$) immersion stations.
2. Integrate ultrasonic/megasonic agitation modules ($1\text{ MHz}$) onto the immersion baths.
3. Torque all flare connections using calibrated torque wrenches according to PFA fitting diameter specifications; perform an initial pneumatic pressure decay integrity check on chemical delivery and gravity drains with dry nitrogen.

#### Step 2: DI Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) & Resistivity Probe Integration
1. Position and level the high-purity virgin PTFE/PVDF Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) vessel within the chemical bench exhaust envelope.
2. Connect Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) supply headers delivering $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ water to the top spray manifolds and bottom fill diffusers.
3. Install the pneumatic bottom dump door mechanism, configuring rapid drain actuation via clean dry air/$\text{N}_2$ solenoid pilots.
4. Mount an in-line high-purity resistivity sensor probe inside the overflow weir/recirculation drain channel to monitor cascade dump-rinse cycles. Set controller logic for automated cascade cycles (5 dump-and-fill cycles minimum).

#### Step 3: High-Purity Filtered $\text{N}_2$ Purge Line Installation
1. Install electro-polished 316L stainless steel or ultra-clean fluoropolymer lines from the bulk nitrogen facility header to point-of-use wet bench drop points.
2. Mount point-of-use $0.05\,\mu\text{m}$ PTFE membrane gas filters immediately upstream of the bench-integrated Marangoni dry heads, manual filtered $\text{N}_2$ blow-off guns, and bath blanket spargers.
3. Connect and calibrate gas flow meters and pressure regulators to supply particle-free $\text{N}_2$ for wafer surface dry and head-space acid vapor displacement.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Inspection / Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **QDR Rinse Endpoint Resistivity** | $> 16$ (Baseline: $18.2$) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line calibrated resistivity conductivity sensor |
| **QDR Cascade Dump Cycle Count** | $5$ | Cycles | Automated PLC recipe counter |
| **RCA-2 Acid Bath Temperature Uniformity** | $75 \pm 2$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion fluoropolymer-encapsulated RTD/thermocouple |
| **Continuous UPW Overflow Duration (Dev/Rinse)** | $60$ | $\text{seconds}$ | Integrated PLC digital sequence timer |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context Alignment

* **RCA-1 (SC-1) & Cascade Dump Rinse Parameters:**  
  * *Citation:* `RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering`  
  * *Context:* 5 cycles cascade dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW until bath resistivity reaches $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$; $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$ immersion bath with $1\text{ MHz}$ megasonic agitation.
* **Native Oxide Strip & RCA-2 (SC-2) Temperature & Drying:**  
  * *Citation:* `RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering`  
  * *Context:* $1:50\text{ to }1:100\text{ HF}$ at $22^\circ\text{C}$; RCA-2 at $75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$; final overflow rinse to $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ followed by filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni/IPA vapor drying.
* **Overflow Dump Rinse Timing & $\text{N}_2$ Dry Integration:**  
  * *Citation:* `Positive Photoresist Spin Dynamics, Soft Bake & Development Protocol`  
  * *Context:* Continuous overflow dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for $60\text{ seconds}$, followed by filtered $\text{N}_2$ drying.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-PFA-002`
## Title: PFA Chemical Delivery Tubing & Multi-Valve Manifold Assembly
**Hierarchy Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & N2 Purge Installation > PFA Chemical Delivery Tubing & Multi-Valve Manifold Assembly  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Cleanroom Class:** ISO 5 (Class 100) Wet Chemistry Bay

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the tooling, assembly sequence, flare-fitting torque specifications, helium/N2 leak testing, and installation of Perfluoroalkoxy (PFA) chemical delivery lines and PTFE/PFA multi-valve manifolds. The assembly feeds corrosive wet-clean chemicals (specifically hot Piranha solution: 3:1 $96\%\,\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 : 30\%\,\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, self-heating up to $110^\circ\text{C}\text{--}130^\circ\text{C}$), DI water rinse, and ultra-high purity (UHP) $N_2$ purge lines servicing the 180nm DRAM capacitor-over-bitline (COB) wafer pre-clean wet bench.

---

### 2. Required Equipment, Materials & PPE

```text
       [ UHP N2 Source (1-5 SLPM) ]
                   │
                   ▼
       [ PFA Multi-Valve Manifold ]
        │         │             │
        ▼         ▼             ▼
   [H2SO4 Line] [H2O2 Line] [Exhaust / Vent]
        │         │             │
        └────┬────┘             ▼
             ▼            [Atmospheric Gas Vent]
    [PTFE Bath: 110-130°C] (Continuous O2/SO2 Evolution)
```

- **Tubing & Fittings:** High-purity electronic-grade PFA fluoropolymer tubing (1/4" and 3/8" OD), PFA Flaretek-style fittings, and PVDF/PFA gripper nuts.
- **Manifold:** High-purity PTFE/PFA pneumatic 2-way and 3-way diaphragm multi-valve distribution manifold.
- **Tools:** Dedicated PFA tube rotary cutter (90° square-cut), heating/flaring mandrel kit, calibrated digital torque wrench with open-ended crowfoot adapters.
- **Safety PPE:** Strict personal protective equipment consisting of heavy neoprene chemical-resistant gloves, full-face poly-carbonate shield, acid/chemical apron, and chemical splash boots over cleanroom bunny suit.
- **Atmospheric Pressure & Venting Accessories:** Unsealed atmospheric pressure relief check valves and vent lines to prevent pressure containment from off-gassing ($O_2, SO_2$).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Assembly Procedure

#### Phase 1: Tube Preparation and Flaring
1. **Square Cut:** Cut the PFA chemical feed tubing to designated lengths using a calibrated PFA rotary shear cutter. Ensure cut face perpendicularity is within $\pm 0.5^\circ$ without burrs, flattening, or swarf.
2. **Nut Insertion:** Slide the PFA/PVDF flare nut over the tubing with threaded orientation facing the cut end.
3. **Flaring:** Insert the tubing end into the heated flaring die/mandrel preheated to the designated polymer softening point. Form a symmetrical bell-flare without visual thinning, bubbling, or longitudinal striations. Allow to cool below $40^\circ\text{C}$ under clean laminar airflow.

#### Phase 2: Manifold & Flare Assembly Installation
1. **Manifold Alignment:** Mount the multi-valve PTFE manifold onto the polypropylene/PTFE wet bench mounting bracket using cleanroom-compatible PFA-coated hardware.
2. **Flare Seating:** Mate the flared tubing end squarely over the male flare body of the multi-valve manifold ports. Ensure concentric alignment without lateral mechanical strain on the manifold body.
3. **Torque Tightening:** Hand-thread the PFA nut until snug. Engage the calibrated crowfoot torque wrench and tighten to the specified manufacturer torque (target: $1.8\text{--}2.2\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ for 1/4" PFA and $3.5\text{--}4.0\,\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ for 3/8" PFA) until full mechanical stop/audible click.

#### Phase 3: Pressure Decay & Carrier Gas Purge Verification
1. **Inert Gas Connection:** Connect the assembly inlet port to the clean carrier gas distribution line regulated by Mass Flow Controllers (MFC) supplying ultra-pure carrier $N_2$.
2. **Purge Sweep:** Initiate a laminar $N_2$ purge through all delivery manifold paths at a flow rate of $1.0\text{ to }5.0\,\text{SLPM}$ for 10 minutes to expel airborne particulates and ambient moisture.
3. **Pressure Proof Test:** Isolate downstream pneumatic diaphragm valves. Pressurize the manifold circuit with dry UHP $N_2$ to $4.0\,\text{bar (gauge)}$ ($400\,\text{kPa}$). Conduct a 30-minute pressure-decay test.
4. **Venting Configuration:** Verify that the chemical line relief and bath exhaust remain vented to the acid scrubber exhaust without closed isolation traps, ensuring continuous dissipation of gases evolved during piranha exothermic mixing ($O_2, SO_2$).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **He/N2 Pressure Decay Rate** | $0.00\,\text{bar/min}$ | $\le 0.02\,\text{bar}$ drop over $30\,\text{min}$ at $4.0\,\text{bar (gauge)}$ | In-line digital pressure transducer data log |
| **Carrier $N_2$ Purge Flow Rate** | $1.0\text{ to }5.0\,\text{SLPM}$ | $\pm 0.1\,\text{SLPM}$ of setpoint | In-line Mass Flow Controller (MFC) feedback |
| **Piranha Solution Thermal Withstand Range** | $110^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }130^\circ\text{C}$ | Maintained without mechanical creep or flare leakage | Infrared pyrometer / immersion thermocouple during chemical qualification run |
| **Line Pressure Containment Mode** | Atmospheric Venting ($0.0\,\text{bar (gauge)}$ backpressure) | Continuous Open Exhaust (Zero sealed storage) | Physical inspection of acid exhaust scrub line / differential pressure sensor ($\Delta P < 5\,\text{Pa}$) |

---

### 5. Context & Literature Citations

1. **Piranha Acid Cleaning Solution Chemistry and Safety Protocols:**
   - *Chemical Formulation:* 3 parts $96\%\,\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to 1 part $30\%\,\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.
   - *Thermal Operating Window:* Spontaneous exothermic reaction heating reaching $110^\circ\text{C}\text{--}130^\circ\text{C}$.
   - *Off-gassing Safety Constraint:* Continuous gas evolution of $O_2$ and $SO_2$; delivery plumbing and receiving bath manifolds must never be locked in sealed configurations.
   - *PPE Protocol:* Mandatory cleanroom acid apron, heavy neoprene gloves, and full face shield.
2. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
   - *Gas Purge Flow Dynamics:* Regulated carrier gas flow regimes utilizing MFCs operating at $1\text{ to }5\,\text{SLPM}$ of $N_2$ purge flow.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)
Piranha Acid Cleaning Solution Chemistry and Safety Protocols (Plummer, Deal, Griffin - Silicon VLSI Technology)

nodes.sop_content:
### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): COTS Pneumatic Dump Gate Valve & Dual-Cascade PTFE Spray Manifold Sourcing and Bench Qualification

**Node Classification**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & N2 Purge Installation > DI Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) & Drain Dump Actuation Integration > COTS Pneumatic Dump Gate Valve & Dual-Cascade PTFE Spray Manifold Sourcing  
**Action Type**: Make / Assembly Integration  
**Generation**: Gen 2 ($\mu$m)

---

#### 1. Workflow Architecture & Visual Lifecycle

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Procurement /     │
│       Sourcing        │
│     Verification      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Dimensional &     │
│       Material        │
│  Compatibility Check  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Dual-Cascade PTFE   │
│       Manifold        │
│     Hydrodynamic      │
│       Benchmark       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Pneumatic Dump Gate  │
│   Actuation & Seal    │
│  Pressure Decay Test  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     DI QDR Basin      │
│  Integration & Drain  │
│     Qualification     │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **COTS Sourcing & Incoming Inspection**:
   - Inspect the incoming COTS pneumatic dump gate valve (PFA/PTFE wetted body with dual-acting pneumatic cylinder) and dual-cascade spray manifolds machined from virgin PTFE.
   - Clean and inspect all components inside a laminar flow clean bench environment using a filtered N₂ blow-off gun to eliminate particulate contamination prior to integration.
2. **Acid Resistance & Material Verification**:
   - Verify that all wetted seals, O-rings, and diaphragm gaskets utilize chemical-duty perfluoroelastomers (FFKM/PTFE) capable of withstanding concentrated acid carryover (e.g., HF, BOE, and hot phosphoric acid $H_3PO_4$ 85% at up to 160°C).
   - Ensure the outer housing and non-wetted hardware are isolated against corrosive acid fumes within the hood exhaust path.
3. **Dual-Cascade PTFE Spray Manifold Calibration**:
   - Plumb high-purity DI water feed lines to the dual-cascade PTFE manifold via flare PFA tubing.
   - Balance spray nozzle distribution to provide uniform, conical laminar sheet wetting over the active wafer boat handling zone.
4. **Pneumatic Actuator Integration & Cycle Validation**:
   - Connect the pneumatic gate actuator to an oil-free, dry $N_2$ / CDA supply line regulated with quick-exhaust solenoid valves.
   - Calibrate the pneumatic stroke cycle for rapid actuation (snap opening/closing) to enable quick-dump draining without cavitation or mechanical binding.
5. **Basin Sealing & Static Hydrostatic Pressure Hold**:
   - Mount the pneumatic dump valve to the bottom drain port of the PTFE quick-dump rinser (QDR) vessel with high-torque chemical flanged fittings.
   - Fill the QDR tank with DI water, pressurize the seat closure under standard actuator line pressure, and conduct a static hydrostatic decay check.

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

- **Quick-Dump Drain Transition Speed**: Dump gate full-open transit time $\le 1.5\text{ s}$ under $60\text{--}80\text{ psi}$ pilot pressure, achieving complete basin drain in $< 5\text{ s}$.
- **Static Seal Leak Rate / Hydrostatic Decay**: $0\text{ mL/min}$ liquid leakage at the dump gate seat under full DI water head ($300\text{ mm}$ static fluid column) over a $30\text{-minute}$ hold period.
- **PTFE Spray Manifold Flow Uniformity & Delivery**: Delivery rate of $8\text{ to }15\text{ SLPM}$ DI water across dual cascade manifolds with nozzle pressure variation $\le \pm 5\%$ across all cascade ports.
- **Corrosion & Acid Etch Stability**: Wetted PTFE/PFA surfaces must maintain dimensional stability with zero chemical degradation and etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ against standard cleanroom acid solutions (dilute HF / BOE equivalents).

---

#### 4. Literature Citations

- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**: Wafer handling, filtered gun cleaning, and rinse particulate management within laminar flow clean bench environments.
- **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**: High chemical resistance baselines, wetted component compatibility benchmarks against concentrated acid chemistries (HF/BOE etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ and hot $H_3PO_4$ 85% at 160°C).

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** QDR Pneumatic Fast-Dump Actuation & Multi-Cycle Fill/Purge Sequence Logic Integration  
**Node Path:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup [Chemical Processing] > Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & N2 Purge Installation [Wet Chemistry] > DI Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) & Drain Dump Actuation Integration [Wet Chemistry] > QDR Pneumatic Fast-Dump Actuation & Multi-Cycle Fill/Purge Sequence Logic Integration [Wet Chemistry]  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Trigger QDR Start   │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  High-Flow Bottom DI  │
│         Fill          │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Active N2 Agitation  │
│       Sparging        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Pneumatic Fast-Dump  │
│         Open          │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│      Sump Drain       │
│     Verification      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Pneumatic Door Seal  │
│         Reset         │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Next Multi-Cycle or  │
│    Final Overflow     │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Check Utilities & Pneumatic Interlocks**
   - Confirm CDA (Clean Dry Air) / N2 supply to the pneumatic solenoid valve block is pressurized.
   - Verify exhaust interlocks at the acid exhaust fume hood and check that the chemical drain line and PFA plumbing are unblocked.
   - Position the cassette containing wafers (subsequent to wet chemical processing such as clean bench RCA baths or hot phosphoric acid/BOE etch sequences) securely onto the QDR PTFE carrier supports.

2. **Pneumatic Bottom-Flap Reset & Sealing**
   - Energize the dump-door pneumatic cylinder via the PLC logic output to pull the bottom elastomeric dump door flush against the PFA sealing seat.
   - Confirm physical closure via magnetic reed / optical proximity position sensors on the cylinder barrel before initiating liquid fill.

3. **High-Flow DI Fill Sequence**
   - Actuate the primary deionized (DI) water proportional valve to flood the tank via bottom manifold distribution jets and overhead cascade nozzles to achieve uniform upward fluid displacement.
   - Fill continuously until the optical or capacitive liquid high-level float switch flags full immersion.

4. **N2 Agitation Purge Sparging**
   - Enable the N2 sparger manifold solenoid valve at the bottom of the tank to introduce fine nitrogen bubbling throughout the wafer cassette slots.
   - Maintain active immersion agitation for the cycle dwell period to break boundary layers and displace residual chemical chemistry from wafer surfaces.

5. **Pneumatic Fast-Dump Actuation**
   - De-energize/switch the dual-action pneumatic dump solenoid, retracting the dump gate to open the bottom cross-section orifice.
   - Facilitate gravitational drop of the water column to strip drag-out liquid off the wafers into the dedicated chemical-resistant drain sump.
   - Validate transition with the optical low-level sensor confirming complete chamber evacuation.

6. **Multi-Cycle Sequencing & Overflow Handshake**
   - Automatically repeat Steps 2 through 5 for the defined multi-cycle recipe count (e.g., 4 to 6 dump cycles).
   - Upon the final cycle, seal the dump gate and transition to top-overflow DI rinse mode. Verify process completion via clean-room bench monitoring before transferring wafers.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Unit | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pneumatic Gate Full-Dump Duration** | $\le 3.0 \pm 0.5$ | $\text{s}$ | PLC cycle timer / Optical sump low-level sensor trip |
| **Chamber DI High-Level Fill Duration** | $\le 15.0 \pm 2.0$ | $\text{s}$ | PLC inline timing register & Capacitive level switch |
| **N2 Agitation Purge Flow Rate** | $1.0\text{ to }5.0$ | $\text{SLPM}$ | Mass Flow Controller (MFC) calibrated readout |
| **Pneumatic Dump Door Actuator Cylinder Stroke Travel** | $\pm 0.5$ | $\text{mm}$ | Linear dial indicator / Mechanical limit switch tolerance |

---

### Relevant Literature Citations

- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
  - Cites the regulation of carrier gas flows (*"N2 purge, ultra-pure O2, or forming gas"* via mass flow controllers at *1 to 5 SLPM*), providing verified gas-flow delivery ranges adaptable to high-purity wafer purge/agitation systems.
- **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
  - Cites wet chemical stripping resistance and downstream processing interfaces (*"etched selectively in hot phosphoric acid (H3PO4 85% at 160°C)"*, *"HF and BOE"*), establishing wet-processing requirements where multi-cycle high-dump flushing is critical to halt residual acid etching.
- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**
  - Cites the integration of filtered spray washdown and clean environment protocols (*"filtered gun inside laminar flow clean bench"*), governing boundary protection during wet clean dump sequencing.

nodes.label: 18.2 MOhm-cm In-Line Resistivity Recovery Metrology & Rinse Efficiency Qualification
nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-MET-002`
**Title:** 18.2 MΩ·cm In-Line Resistivity Recovery Metrology & Rinse Efficiency Qualification  
**Module:** Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > DI Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) & Drain Dump Actuation Integration  
**Generation Target:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Buy / In-Line Metrology Integration  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Visual Flow

In 180nm DRAM fabrication (stacked capacitor over bitline architectures with wet etching/stripping such as hot phosphoric acid nitride removal), residual ionic acid species degrade dielectric interfaces and promote junction/sub-threshold leakage. This procedure governs the qualification of the in-line resistivity cell (temperature-compensated at 25°C) mounted in the QDR overflow cascade drain to ensure rapid rinse recovery to baseline UPW (Ultra-Pure Water) resistivity (18.2 MΩ·cm).

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Acid Bath Cassette   │
│       Transfer        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   QDR Primary Fast    │
│      Dump Cycle       │◄─╮
└───────────┬───────────┘  │
            │              │
            ▼              │
┌───────────────────────┐  │
│  Cascade Resistivity  │  │
│     In-Line Flow      │  │
└───────────┬───────────┘  │
            │              │No
            ▼              │
┌───────────────────────┐  │
│   Resistivity Probe   │  │
│      Measurement      │  │
└───────────┬───────────┘  │
            │              │
            ▼              │
┌───────────◇───────────┐  │
│     18.2 MOhm-cm      ├──╯
│  Baseline Recovery?   │
└───────────◇───────────┘
            │
         Yes│
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  N2 Knife Final Dry   │
│     Qualification     │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Check & In-Line Sensor Baseline Calibration:**
   - Verify continuous UPW supply pressure to the wet bench PTFE/PFA manifold (30 to 45 psig).
   - Ensure the in-line PFA flow-through resistivity sensor (cell constant $K = 0.01\text{ cm}^{-1}$ or $0.05\text{ cm}^{-1}$ with integral Pt1000 RTD) is bubble-free and reads UPW baseline resistivity $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ normalized to 25°C.
   - Confirm pneumatic bottom-dump actuator valve responds in $< 1.5\text{ s}$ without leakage under full static head.

2. **Cassette Loading & Transfer Post-Acid Strip:**
   - Transfer wafer carrier from the acid process tank (e.g., $85\%\text{ H}_3\text{PO}_4$ nitride etch bath operating at $160^\circ\text{C}$ or BOE clean) into the QDR chamber via PTFE-sheathed transfer mechanism.
   - Minimize transfer transit air exposure to $< 5\text{ s}$ to prevent ionic drying and crystallization on wafer topologies.

3. **Pneumatic Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) Cycling:**
   - Trigger the automated QDR recipe:
     - **Fill Step:** High-flow DI top-spray and bottom-manifold fill until water level covers top of cassette sensors ($< 15\text{ s}$).
     - **Quick-Dump Step:** Rapid bottom pneumatic flap valve dump actuated ($< 2.5\text{ s}$ complete evacuation).
     - Run 4 consecutive dump-and-fill cycles to dilute bulk acid carry-over.

4. **Continuous Cascade Overflow & In-Line Resistivity Monitoring:**
   - Transition QDR from dump mode to laminar bottom-up cascade overflow.
   - Direct overflow stream past the in-line PFA resistivity flow cell.
   - Record time-dependent resistivity trace: track initial ionic dip ($< 1.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) recovering toward $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

5. **Rinse End-Point Detection & Transfer Lockout:**
   - The automated recipe controller evaluates real-time effluent resistivity.
   - Verify rinse reaches $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ within specified recovery time budget ($< 120\text{ s}$ cascade phase).
   - Once stable at $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ for $\ge 30\text{ s}$, trigger N2 purge blanket and unlock cassette hoist for transfer to the drying/LPCVD stage.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Tolerance | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Effluent UPW Resistivity Baseline** | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ | In-line PFA flow-through resistivity sensor with 4-wire Pt1000 RTD |
| **Resistivity Recovery Time ($t_{\text{rec}}$)** | $< 120\text{ s}$ | $\pm 5\text{ s}$ | Automated PLC recipe timer from cascade switch to $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ |
| **QDR Pneumatic Bottom-Dump Actuation Speed** | $< 2.5\text{ s}$ | $\pm 0.3\text{ s}$ | Hall-effect cylinder stroke position sensors & drain pressure switch |
| **Total QDR Water Evacuation Volume Rate** | Full dump in $< 2.5\text{ s}$ | Evacuation efficiency $\ge 99.5\%$ | Optical liquid level float sensors (chamber empty flag) |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:**
  - *Context:* Wet processing selective etch occurs in hot phosphoric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ $85\%$ at $160^\circ\text{C}$); HF and BOE etch resistance ($< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$). Residual phosphoric and fluoride residues mandate rapid QDR cycle dumps before surface repassivation.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Context:* $180\text{ nm}$ technology node ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$); capacitor budget of minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$ with leakage current target kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$. Incomplete rinsing of conductive ionic trace contaminants across bitline contacts and stacked crown capacitors directly degrades retention time and increases sub-threshold/junction leakage.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** Ultra-High Purity N2 Purge Line & Resistivity Rinse Metrology Verification  
**Module:** Wet Chemistry / Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup  
**Technology Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology & Facility Verification  

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Start: N2 & UPW Line  │
│      Verification      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Step 1: UHP N2 Purge  │
│  Line Leak & Particle  │
│   Cleanliness Check    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Step 2: QDR       │
│   Resistivity Sensor   │
│     Calibration &      │
│  Baseline Drift Test   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Step 3: Dynamic     │
│   5-Cycle Quick-Dump   │
│   Rinse Verification   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────◇───────────┐
│   Resistivity >= 16    │
│    MΩ·cm at 25°C?      │
└────────────◇───────────┘
     │               │
   No│               │Yes
     ▼               ▼
┌────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐
│ Purge & Retest │ │ Sign-off: Ready for    │
│ UPW Loop       │ │ 180nm RCA Clean Baseline│
└────────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **UHP $\text{N}_2$ Purge Supply Line Integrity & Flow Rate Verification**
   - Verify supply line source purity ($99.9999\%$ Grade UHP $\text{N}_2$) through point-of-use PFA particle filtration.
   - Pressurize the PTFE bench $\text{N}_2$ purge lines to $2.5\text{ bar}$ gauge; hold for $15\text{ minutes}$ to confirm zero pressure drop ($\Delta P = 0.00\text{ bar}$).
   - Set the $\text{N}_2$ blanket purge to the quick-dump rinser (QDR) and acid bath headspace at $10\text{ to }15\text{ SLPM}$ laminar blanket flow.

2. **Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) Resistivity Sensor Metrology Calibration**
   - Calibrate the inline/immersion toroidal conductivity/resistivity cell against temperature-compensated NIST-traceable standard cells at $25.0^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Supply baseline Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) into the QDR chamber and verify incoming water reaches the physical maximum theoretical target of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

3. **Dynamic Dump Rinse Cycle & Resistivity Recovery Test**
   - Initiate a sequence of **$5\text{ automated dump-and-fill cycles}$** in the QDR.
   - Monitor the effluent dump resistivity at each cycle: ensure rapid filling and bottom-dump evacuation under continuous top-spray UPW.
   - Verify that following chemical carry-over testing (post alkaline oxidation/SC-1 bath simulation), the bath returns to a resistivity threshold $> 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ before the 5th cycle concludes.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │░░░░░░░░░                     │
              QDR Cycles┤░░░░░░░░░                     │
                        │▒                             │
    UHP N2 Filter Rating┤▒                             │
Cascade Dump Resistivity┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
                        │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓    │
  Target UPW Resistivity┤██████████████████████████████│
                        │██████████████████████████████│
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                        0.0    4.5     9.1   13.6  18.2 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Threshold | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Metrology |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Incoming UPW Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (at $25^\circ\text{C}$) | Inline temperature-compensated resistivity sensor |
| **Cascade Dump Rinse Resistivity** | $> 16.0$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | QDR effluent bath resistivity probe |
| **Cascade Rinse Cycle Count** | $\le 5$ | $\text{cycles}$ | Automated QDR PLC controller |
| **Point-of-Use $\text{N}_2$ Particulate Filtration** | $\le 0.05$ | $\mu\text{m}$ retention rating | PFA membrane gas line filter |

---

### Literature Citations & Traceability
- **RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering**:
  - Validates the baseline supply of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ Ultra-Pure Water (UPW).
  - Establishes the exact cascade dump rinse specification: *5 cycles with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water until bath resistivity $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$* to eliminate sub-micron particles via zeta potential control prior to high-temperature furnace operations.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench** & **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**:
  - Enforces contamination control required to prevent excessive junction leakage ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) and preserve retention ($> 64\text{ ms}$ for $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ cell capacitance across the $3.5\text{ nm}$ gate oxide and $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ capacitor dielectric stacks).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-UHP-N2-001`
**Title:** UHP $\text{N}_2$ Gas Distribution Manifold & In-Line Particle Filtration Assembly  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & $\text{N}_2$ Purge Installation > Ultra-High Purity $\text{N}_2$ Purge Line & Resistivity Rinse Metrology Verification > UHP $\text{N}_2$ Gas Distribution Manifold & In-Line Particle Filtration Assembly  
**Generation:** Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Architecture Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  UHP N2 Source Supply  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        316L VCR        │
│      Distribution      │
│        Manifold        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   0.003 um Sintered    │
│    PTFE/SS In-Line     │
│         Filter         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Pneumatic Isolation   │
│    Diaphragm Valve     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Laminar Flow MFC    │
│   Delivery 1-5 SLPM    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wet Chemistry Bench   │
│     & Purge Drops      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Installation Component Inspection & Cleanroom Preparation**
   - Stage 316L VAR/VIM electropolished stainless steel manifold blocks, face-seal VCR fittings, and point-of-use (POU) in-line particle filters in an ISO Class 4 cleanroom environment.
   - Inspect sealing glands and silver-plated nickel gaskets under optical magnification; reject any fitting with circumferential or radial scratching on face-seal beads.

2. **Manifold Sub-Assembly & Torque Spec Verification**
   - Assemble the distribution manifold block by hand-tightening 1/4" VCR female nuts onto male glands with clean nickel gaskets installed.
   - Secure the manifold in an assembly fixture; use calibrated dual-wrench counter-torque to advance VCR nuts $1/8$ turn past finger-tight (or $13.5\text{ to }16.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$).

3. **In-Line Particle Filtration Integration**
   - Integrate the all-metal/PTFE sintered point-of-use gas filter directly downstream of the manifold primary isolation valve.
   - Verify flow direction indicator arrow matches the delivery vector toward the wet chemical bench quick-dump rinser (QDR) and acid bath blanket purge.

4. **Helium Leak Metrology (Outboard & Inboard)**
   - Connect a calibrated Helium Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (MSLD) to the manifold vacuum port.
   - Evacuate manifold to $< 10\text{ mTorr}$ and perform inboard helium spray probe verification across all mechanical VCR joints and weld seams.
   - Pressurize the assembly to $1.5\times$ working line pressure with helium/nitrogen trace gas and perform outboard sniffing around filter flanges.

5. **Hot High-Velocity Purge & Flow Calibration via MFC**
   - Couple the manifold inlet to certified Ultra-High Purity (UHP) $\text{N}_2$ source gas.
   - Execute cyclic pressure-purge venting (50 cycles between $0.1\text{ MPa}$ and $0.5\text{ MPa}$).
   - Set the Mass Flow Controller (MFC) to regulate carrier gas flow through delivery branches within **1 to 5 SLPM** laminar delivery mode.

6. **Condensation, Particle Counter & Metrology Validation**
   - Connect an aerosol condensation particle counter (CPC) downstream of the filter exhaust.
   - Verify background counts are zero at the target sensitivity threshold prior to sign-off and plumb delivery lines directly to PTFE bench baths and quick-dump rinse purge ports.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Exact Tolerance / Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Carrier Gas Mass Flow Rate** | $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$ | $\pm 1.0\%\text{ of Full Scale}$ | Thermal Mass Flow Controller (MFC) calibrated output |
| **Helium Leak Integrity** | $< 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ mbar}\cdot\text{L/s}$ | Upper Bound Threshold ($\text{He}$) | Mass Spectrometer Leak Detector (MSLD) inboard vacuum mode |
| **POU In-Line Particle Filtration Retention** | $99.9999999\%\text{ (9-nines) at }\ge 0.003\ \mu\text{m}$ | $0\text{ counts/standard cubic foot at }\ge 0.1\ \mu\text{m}$ | Cleanroom Condensation Particle Counter (CPC) |
| **Manifold Working Pressure Retention** | $0.40\text{ MPa}\text{ (4.0 bar static)}$ | $\Delta P \le 1.0\text{ kPa / hr}$ over 24 hrs | High-accuracy digital piezoresistive gauge transducer |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Reference Context

- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
  - *Extracted Data & Constraints:* Gas Flow Dynamics specify carrier gases ($\text{N}_2$ purge, ultra-pure $\text{O}_2$, or forming gas) regulated by mass flow controllers (MFC) at **1 to 5 SLPM** with laminar flow dynamics. Used to define the primary manifold delivery throughput and flow controller scaling.
- **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
  - *Extracted Data & Constraints:* Regulates clean carrier/dilution gas delivery regimes, pressure boundaries, and isolation from chemical-duty mechanical vacuum systems and acid wet-processing interfaces.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Extracted Data & Constraints:* Stringent particulate limits and dielectric breakdown considerations at $180\text{ nm}$ geometry (critical dimension scale $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) requiring strict sub-micron filtration to avoid killer defects during capacitor and dielectric stack fabrication.
citations: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)
Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks (Kern & Rosler - Chemically Vapor Deposited Synthetic Materials)

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** DI Quick-Dump Rinser 18.2 MΩ·cm Resistivity Recovery & Ionic Carryover Qualification  
**Module:** Wet Chemistry / Metrology  
**Node Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Crown/Cylinder Stacked Capacitor & Gate Dielectric Processing)  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure qualifies the operational performance of the Deionized Water (DIW) Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) installed in the acid wet bench. It verifies baseline resistivity recovery to theoretical purity (18.2 MΩ·cm at 25°C) and measures the elimination of ionic carryover (specifically residual chemical ions following wet etching/cleaning steps such as hot $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ nitride strip or gate pre-cleans) to prevent contamination of thin gate oxides (~3.5 nm) and storage capacitor dielectrics (EOT 3–4 nm).

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Materials
- High-purity PFA Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) tank equipped with bottom pneumatically actuated dump door and top/bottom DIW spray nozzles.
- In-line PFA conductivity/resistivity sensor and meter (calibrated, temperature-compensated to 25°C, cell constant $k = 0.01\ \text{cm}^{-1}$).
- Ultra-High Purity (UHP) $\text{N}_2$ source for bubbler agitation and pneumatic actuation.
- Test quartz or virgin PTFE wafer carrier loaded with 150mm/200mm dummy silicon monitor wafers.
- Chemical carryover test solution (85% $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ or dilute clean chemistries simulating capacitor nitride etch/pre-gate clean).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------+     +-----------------------+     +-----------------------+
|  1. Static Baseline   | --> | 2. Dynamic QDR Cycles | --> |  3. Resistivity &     |
|   Resistivity Check   |     |   (Spray/Fill/Dump)   |     |   Carryover Log       |
+-----------------------+     +-----------------------+     +-----------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Static Baseline Verification
1. Ensure the acid fume hood exhaust is active and laminar flow velocity is stable.
2. Fill the QDR tank with continuous UPW (Ultra-Pure Water) until overflow occurs.
3. Turn on the in-line UPW resistivity monitoring system.
4. Verify UPW supply line reads $\ge 18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ for a minimum stabilization window of 5 minutes before wafer immersion.

#### Step 2: Mechanical Quick-Dump & Refill Sequence Setup
1. Program the PLC/controller recipe for a standard 4-cycle dump-and-fill sequence:
   - **Spray Step:** Top spray active for 15 seconds during drain.
   - **Dump Step:** Bottom pneumatic dump valve opens, draining the full volume in $\le 5$ seconds.
   - **Fill Step:** Fast bottom/top fill, reaching overflow level in $\le 20$ seconds.
   - **Purge Step:** Ultra-High Purity $\text{N}_2$ bubbler assist activated during fill to enhance convective displacement of stagnant boundary layer fluid between adjacent wafers (maintaining pitch spacing of 360–400 nm equivalent wafer clearance).

#### Step 3: Ionic Carryover Challenge Test
1. Load dummy wafer cassette into the chemical bath (e.g., simulating hot $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ dip or pre-gate oxide clean).
2. Allow a 30-second dwell time, followed by standard 10-second drip over the chemical bath.
3. Transfer cassette smoothly via automated or manual arm into the QDR chamber within 5 seconds to prevent drying/crystallization on wafer surfaces.
4. Trigger the automated QDR recipe (4 dump cycles followed by continuous UPW overflow cascade).

#### Step 4: Endpoint Detection & Resistivity Recovery Logging
1. Engage the in-line cell during the overflow cascade phase.
2. Log the time elapsed ($T_{\text{recovery}}$) from initial cascade start until resistivity recovers from baseline depression to $> 18.0\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ and plateaus at $\ge 18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
3. Record peak ionic depression, final rinse temperature ($25^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$), and total water volume consumed per qualification run.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Terminal UPW Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (at $25^\circ\text{C}$) | In-line temperature-compensated resistivity sensor |
| **Resistivity Recovery Time ($T_{\text{recovery}}$)** | $\le 120$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated PLC timer from overflow onset to $\ge 18.0\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ |
| **QDR Tank Fast Dump Duration** | $\le 5.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Optical/conductive drain sensor threshold |
| **QDR Tank Fill Duration** | $\le 20.0$ | $\text{s}$ | High-level float/optical sensor trigger |

---

### 5. Context & Literature Citations

- **Source: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench***
  - *Context:* Strict ionic clean requirements safeguard the stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architecture and access transistor channels ($L = 180\ \text{nm}$, $W = 220\ \text{nm}$) to preserve low leakage current ($< 1\ \text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$) and target cell capacitance ($\ge 28\ \text{fF}$).
- **Source: *Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks***
  - *Context:* Effective DIW rinsing and rapid dumping prevent ionic residue carryover from concentrated $\text{HF/BOE}$ cleans and hot phosphoric acid ($85\%\ \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ at $160^\circ\text{C}$) used for selective $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ removal.
- **Source: *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering***
  - *Context:* 1T1C cells with gate dielectrics of $\sim 3.5\ \text{nm}$ physical thickness grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ and capacitor dielectrics with equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) of $3\text{--}4\ \text{nm}$ demand ultra-pure rinse endpoints ($18.2\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$) to prevent mobile ion dielectric breakdown.
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks (Kern & Rosler - Chemically Vapor Deposited Synthetic Materials)
Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering (IEEE / Legacy Foundry Technical Reports)

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-WET-180NM-MET-001
**Title:** Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm)  
**Action Type:** Buy / Facility & Wet Bench Certification  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the exact calibration and certification protocols for wet chemical processing benches (PTFE wet deck and acid exhaust hoods) utilized in the cleaning, etching, and pre-furnace surface preparation for 180nm DRAM fabrication (e.g., gate oxide pre-clean, ONO/high-$\kappa$ capacitor dielectric wet cleans, bitline contact de-glaze). This ensures full acid vapor containment, cleanroom safety, laminar capture velocity, and Ultra-Pure Deionized (DI) water resistivity compliance.

---

### 2. Required Metrology Equipment & Standards
- **Vane / Hot-Wire Anemometer:** Calibrated NIST-traceable digital thermal anemometer (resolution $\pm 0.01\text{ m/s}$ or $\pm 2\text{ FPM}$).
- **Non-Toxic Smoke / Vapor Generator:** Titanium tetrachloride-free glycol/DI fog generator or dry-ice/DI smoke pencil for flow visualization.
- **In-Line / Handheld DI Resistivity Metrology:** Temperature-compensated conductivity/resistivity cell calibrated to ASTM D1125 / SEMI standard ($25.0^\circ\text{C}$ reference).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Calibration & Certification Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 1: Face Velocity Grid Mapping (Fume Hood Sash Opening) |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 2: Acid Vapor Containment Smoke Visualization Test     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 3: Deionized (DI) Water Point-of-Use Resistivity Check |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Face Velocity Grid Calibration
1. Position the fume hood vertical sash at the standard certified operating sash opening height ($18\text{ inches}$ or $457\text{ mm}$).
2. Subdivide the open face area into an imaginary equal-area grid of cells not exceeding $1\text{ sq ft}$ ($0.09\text{ m}^2$) each (minimum $3 \times 3$ grid points).
3. Mount the calibrated hot-wire/vane anemometer probe at the center of each grid position, facing perpendicular to the incoming cleanroom air stream.
4. Measure and log average velocity over $10\text{ seconds}$ per point:
   - Average face velocity target: $100\text{ FPM} \pm 10\%$ ($0.51\text{ m/s} \pm 0.05\text{ m/s}$).
   - Calculate face velocity uniformity: No individual grid measurement shall deviate by more than $\pm 20\%$ from the average face velocity.
5. If velocity is out of range, adjust the acid exhaust damper valve at the bench exhaust plenum until compliant, then lock the damper collar.

#### Step 2: Acid Vapor Containment & Flow Visualization (Per ASHRAE 110 / SEMI S2)
1. Set the vapor/smoke generator at the bench work surface $6\text{ inches}$ ($150\text{ mm}$) inside the sash line.
2. Traverse the smoke wand across the perimeter, side baffles, and rear exhaust slots at a rate of $1\text{ ft/s}$ ($0.3\text{ m/s}$).
3. Visually inspect flow dynamics:
   - Verify smooth, laminar flow drawn straight into the rear exhaust slots and bottom baffles.
   - Confirm zero smoke roll-out, turbulence vortices, or escape toward the operator breathing zone under active exhaust.
4. Simulate operator movement by moving a dummy panel across the sash face to ensure face velocity capture is robust against walk-by wake effects.

#### Step 3: DI Water Resistivity Certification (Point-of-Use Quick-Dump Rinsers & Bath Lines)
1. Open the Point-of-Use (POU) ultra-pure DI water supply valve at the PTFE wet bench and flush into the drain/QDR (Quick-Dump Rinser) for $\ge 5\text{ minutes}$ to displace stagnant line volume.
2. Read the calibrated temperature-compensated inline sensor or extract a sample using a clean PTFE beaker with immediate insertion of the certified probe.
3. Verify that the resistivity stabilizes at $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25.0^\circ\text{C}$ (spec limit $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ for ultra-pure final rinse).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Metrology Instrument | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Pass/Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Average Face Velocity** | Calibrated Hot-Wire Anemometer | $100\text{ FPM}$ ($0.51\text{ m/s}$) | $\pm 10\text{ FPM}$ ($90 - 110\text{ FPM}$ / $0.46 - 0.56\text{ m/s}$) | Mandatory Pass |
| **Velocity Point Uniformity** | Multi-point Grid Scan | $\le 15\%$ Deviation | Max $\pm 20\%$ per grid point | Mandatory Pass |
| **Vapor Containment Escape** | Smoke Generator Visual Flow Test | $0\text{ roll-out}$ | Zero visible fume leakage past sash line | Mandatory Pass |
| **POU DI Water Resistivity** | Temperature-Compensated Resistivity Meter | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ | Minimum $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Mandatory Pass |

  - *Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* — Dry oxidation gate dielectric ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$) and high-$\kappa$ capacitor cleans require stringent ionic contamination control and absolute cleanroom vapor containment to avoid device degradation and defectivity.
  - *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* — Stacked capacitor formation with high-$\kappa$ ($Ta_2O_5 / Al_2O_3$ or ONO) dielectric requires ultraclean surface preparation with ultra-pure DI rinsing to maintain leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Anemometer Traverse Grid Setup & Multi-Point Baseline Profiling

**Node Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Parent Chain:** Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup → Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification → Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Classification:** Metrology / Facility Aerodynamics & Containment  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│           Traverse Grid Fixture Installation           │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│       Thermal Anemometer Insertion & Zero-Offset       │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│         Multi-Point Face Velocity Profiling            │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│       VAV Dynamic Response & Profile Acceptance        │
│                                                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Sash Height and Plane Definition**:
   - Set the acid exhaust fume hood sash to its standard certified working aperture height.
   - Secure a non-intrusive traverse grid frame across the sash opening plane, dividing the entrance cross-section into equal rectangular grid cells (maximum grid point spacing $\le 300\text{ mm}$ center-to-center).

2. **Thermal Anemometer Fixturing & Directional Alignment**:
   - Mount the calibrated thermal anemometer probe on the mechanical traverse rig at normal incidence ($90^\circ \pm 2^\circ$) perpendicular to the sash face plane.
   - Confirm zero-velocity shield caps are seated during initial electronic thermal baseline compensation and zero-point calibration.

3. **Multi-Point Grid Traverse & Dwell Measurement**:
   - Position the thermal anemometer sensor at the geometric center of each traverse cell.
   - Maintain a minimum dwell time of 15 seconds per grid point to allow the heated sensor bead to reach thermal equilibrium with the incoming laminar air velocity.
   - Record the time-averaged face velocity at each point across the top, middle, and bottom horizontal planes.

4. **Dynamic Aerodynamic Profile & Turbulence Mapping**:
   - Traverse the thermal sensor across all perimeter and central nodes to compute velocity uniformity:
     $$\text{Uniformity} = \frac{V_{\text{max}} - V_{\text{min}}}{2 \times V_{\text{avg}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Check lower sash boundary and aerofoil sill zones for back-draft eddies or dead zones.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric / Tolerance | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Grid Traverse Spacing** | $\le 300$ | $\text{mm}$ | Calibrated precision traverse rail scale |
| **Average Face Velocity ($V_{\text{avg}}$)** | $0.50 \pm 0.05$ ($100 \pm 10$) | $\text{m/s}$ ($\text{fpm}$) | Multi-point time-averaged thermal anemometry |
| **Velocity Uniformity Spread** | $\le \pm 15\%$ of mean across grid points | $\%$ | Multi-point grid calculation |
| **Sensor Measurement Dwell Time** | $\ge 15.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated data logger acquisition timer |

---

### 4. Relevant Literature Citations

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - Informs the critical multi-point profiling methodology, sensor dwell stabilization, and spatial boundary uniformity targets across dimensioned zones (counteracting convective end-losses and ensuring cross-sectional profile fidelity within dimensional bounds $\le 300\text{ mm}$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering** & **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Contextualizes contamination containment standards for cleanroom acid wet benches used during 180nm capacitor dielectric cleaning/etching (ONO, $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), where face velocity stability prevents toxic vapor back-diffusion and particulate deposition onto active bitline/transistor surfaces.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** VAV Damper Actuator PID Tuning & Aerodynamic Baffle Real-Time Calibration  
**Hierarchy Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification > Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning > VAV Damper Actuator PID Tuning & Aerodynamic Baffle Real-Time Calibration  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Baffle Slit       │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Actuator Step      │
│        Response        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Triple Loop PID     │
│         Tuning         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Face Velocity      │
│  Profile Verification  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Calibration & Physical Alignment Setup**
   - Inspect PTFE bench containment enclosure and verify the rear aerodynamic exhaust baffles are unblocked.
   - Set top and bottom aerodynamic baffle slit apertures symmetrically across the full 300 mm lateral zone to distribute cross-draft resistance evenly.
   - Power on the VAV motorized damper actuator control module and establish communication with the digital control interface.

2. **Step-Response Excitation & Actuator Velocity Limiting**
   - Introduce a step change command across the damper travel range (0% to 100% stroke).
   - Ensure the actuator ramp rate is mechanically clamped to prevent abrupt draft surges or structural strain, maintaining smooth mechanical actuation (< 50 mm/minute equivalent drive rate).
   - Record open-loop dead time ($\tau_d$) and time constant ($\tau$) from differential pressure and velocity feedback transmitters.

3. **Digital Triple-Loop PID Tuning with Feedforward Decoupling**
   - Configure a triple-loop digital PID algorithm incorporating feedforward decoupling:
     - **Proportional Gain ($K_p$):** Increment until rapid displacement response is reached without deadband hunting.
     - **Integral Time ($T_i$):** Tune to eliminate residual steady-state draft offset under continuous carrier exhaust conditions.
     - **Derivative Time ($T_d$):** Adjust to suppress transient overshoot and damp pressure fluctuations.
   - Verify decoupling across multi-zone exhaust pickup points to isolate turbulence caused by varying laboratory static pressures.

4. **Real-Time Aerodynamic Baffle Optimization & Dynamic Verification**
   - Adjust the aerodynamic baffle slit positioning dynamically while simulating exhaust thermal loads (such as hot acid baths at 160°C).
   - Modulate carrier gas flow rates from 1 to 5 SLPM into the bench exhaust plenum to ensure laminar air entrainment across the sash boundary.
   - Validate that transient damper corrections maintain stable containment without causing crystallographic disturbance or particle back-streaming into the bench work area.

---

### Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
               Process Control Target Acceptance
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
H3PO4 Etch Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
               │█                                      │
Thermal Uniform┤█                                      │
  Gas Flow Ctrl┤▒▒                                     │
               │▒▒                                     │
Step Travel Spd┤█████████████                          │
               │█████████████                          │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
                0        40       80        120     160 
```

1. **Actuator Linear Motion Limit:** Travel/ramp speed must not exceed **50 mm/minute** (`< 50 mm/minute`) to prevent mechanical shock and aerodynamic pressure spikes.
2. **Carrier Gas Dynamics Regulation:** Damper control loop must dynamically stabilize carrier flow disturbances spanning **1 to 5 SLPM**.
3. **Thermal Environment Uniformity:** Steady-state regulation must support tight thermal isolation within **±0.5°C** across a **300 mm** operational flat zone.
4. **Thermal Exhaust Containment Compatibility:** The calibrated VAV extraction must safely handle continuous acid vapor generation at **160°C** (phosphoric acid $H_3PO_4$ 85% processing condition).

---

### Verified Context Citations

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - *PID Control:* Triple-loop digital PID controller with feedforward decoupling.
  - *Actuator Motion & Shock Prevention:* Mechanical drive speed regulated to `< 50 mm/minute` to avoid mechanical dislocations and shock.
  - *Temperature Uniformity & Span:* Uniformity within `±0.5°C` over a `300 mm` zone.
  - *Gas Flow Dynamics:* Carrier gas flows regulated between `1 to 5 SLPM`.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:
  - *Acid Wet Chemistry Exhaust Conditions:* Selective wet chemical etching of nitride masks in hot phosphoric acid (`H3PO4 85% at 160°C`), setting the thermal acid vapor loading requirement.

Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects (Vossen & Kern - Thin Film Processes)

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-FUME-002`
**Title:** ASHRAE 110 Face Velocity Containment Verification & Dynamic Sash Metrology Certification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification > Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Buy (Procurement & Certification Protocol)  
**Target Environment:** Acid Etch Bench / Wet Chemical Processing Area  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP outlines the protocol for verifying face velocity containment, dynamic sash aerodynamic response, and tracer gas certification under ANSI/ASHRAE 110 standards for acid exhaust fume hoods and PTFE chemical wet benches. This certification ensures chemical vapor containment during wet-chemical cleaning, oxide stripping, and photolithography wet development steps (e.g., Shipley 1813 / MF-319 wet processing) for Gen 2 DRAM fabrication.

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Metrology Tools
- **Thermal Anemometer (Hot-wire / Vane):** Calibrated velocity grid meter (0.01 m/s resolution).
- **Tracer Gas Injection System:** Pure Sulfur Hexafluoride ($SF_6$) delivery manifold with critical flow orifice set to 4.0 L/min.
- **Gas Analyzer:** Electron Capture Detector (ECD) or Miran SapphIRe portable infrared gas analyzer (0.01 ppm detection limit).
- **Dynamic Sash Metrology Rig:** Linear displacement sensor with encoder to measure sash travel speed and response latency.
- **Titanium Tetrachloride / Glycol Fog Generator:** Neutral-buoyancy visual smoke tracer.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Test Inspection & Mechanical Zeroing
1. Inspect the fume hood aerodynamic airfoil, rear baffle positions, and PTFE sash tracks for obstructions or particulate accumulation.
2. Confirm the laboratory supply HVAC systems are in steady-state operation with no direct air currents (> 0.15 m/s) impinging within 1.5 m of the hood face.
3. Level and zero the dynamic sash displacement sensor rig.

#### Step 2: Grid-Based Face Velocity Profile Measurement
1. Position the sash at the certified operational working height (typically 450 mm / 18 inches).
2. Establish a multi-point imaginary grid across the sash opening (measuring points spaced at centers of equal areas, $\le 300\text{ mm} \times 300\text{ mm}$).
3. Clamp the thermal anemometer at each grid node and record the 20-second average face velocity.
4. Calculate the average face velocity and the percentage deviation across all grid positions.

#### Step 3: Flow Visualization & Airfoil Boundary Layer Verification
1. Introduce low-velocity neutral-buoyancy smoke along the bottom airfoil, perimeter jambs, and interior rear baffles.
2. Verify smoke moves smoothly across the work surface into the lower exhaust slot without vortex roll-out or boundary layer separation.
3. Traverse smoke along the sash handle and upper opening edge to check for vortex shedding.

#### Step 4: Tracer Gas Containment Testing ($SF_6$)
1. Mount the ASHRAE 110 ejector 300 mm behind the sash face on the centerline of the PTFE bench.
2. Mount the mannequin and sampling probe 75 mm in front of the sash plane at typical operator breathing height.
3. Release $SF_6$ tracer gas at a stabilized flow rate of 4.0 L/min.
4. Log continuous concentration readings over a 5-minute sampling interval under static sash conditions.

#### Step 5: Dynamic Sash Movement Effect (VAV Metrology)
1. Actuate the sash from fully closed to the maximum certified design height and return to closed position at a controlled mechanical travel speed.
2. Measure the variable air volume (VAV) exhaust dampener response time and record peak tracer leakage during rapid dynamic movement cycles.
3. Ensure no concentration spikes breach allowable exposure control limits during sash transitions.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Limit | Exact Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Average Face Velocity** | $0.50$ | $\pm 0.05$ (Grid Uniformity $\le \pm 10\%$) | $\text{m/s}$ (meters per second) |
| **ASHRAE 110 Containment Rating** | $\le 0.05$ | Maximum control level | $\text{ppm}$ ($SF_6$ tracer leakage) |
| **VAV Aerodynamic Response Time** | $\le 3.0$ | Time to restore $0.50\text{ m/s}$ face velocity | $\text{s}$ (seconds) |
| **Dynamic Sash Travel Speed** | $\le 50$ | Controlled testing speed | $\text{mm/minute}$ |

---

### 5. Verified Local Literature Citations
- **[Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)]**: Referenced for photolithography wet-chemical processing context, establishing developer containment protocols (Microposit MF-319 developer wet-bench processing and DI rinse cycles) and Gen 2 micro-scale alignment tolerances ($\pm 5\text{ \mu m}$).
- **[Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation]**: Referenced for standardized slow mechanical stage motion and linear velocity handling limits ($< 50\text{ mm/minute}$) used as the benchmark rate for controlled displacement metrology rigs.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Referenced for wafer unit-level cleanroom environmental and chemical purity constraints associated with Gen 2 DRAM wet dielectric etch steps (ONO stack and Ta2O5 / Al2O3 high-k deposition preparation).
citations: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench (Kang & Leblebici - CMOS Digital Integrated Circuits)
Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation (Levinson - Principles of Lithography & Thermal Processing)
Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018) (https://sam.zeloof.xyz/first-ic/)
